label: thm:introN1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:introN1}
Let $n\ge2$ and let $F'/K$ be a finite extension with $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes_KF')\le1$. Then $[F':K]\ge p^{n-1}$. Hence $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ge2$ for $d<p^{n-1}$, $d_1(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=p^{n-1}$ and $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ge p^{n-1}+1$, for all $p$ and $n\ge2$.
head: environment

label: thm:introptp
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:introptp}
Let $n\ge2$ and let $F'/K$ be a finite extension of degree prime to $p$ with $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes_KF')\le1$. Then $[F':K]\ge l_n(p)$. Hence $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=l_n(p)=(p^{2n-1}+1)/(p+1)$ for all $p$ and $n\ge2$.
head: environment

label: rem:dependsramif
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:dependsramif}
The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:introptp} uses the ramification theory of cyclic covers of $k((x))$ in exactly two places, both quoted: (i) the upper breaks of the Artin--Schreier--Witt cover $\overline{U}_n\to\mathbb{P}^1_t$ of class $[t]$ are $1,p,\dots,p^{n-1}$, which gives the value of $l_n(p)$, the genus of $\overline{U}_{n-1}$ and the upper bound (the cover is defined over $\mathbb{F}_p$ and lower breaks do not change under the constant field extension $\mathbb{F}_p((1/t))\subset k((1/t))$, so the formula for a finite residue field suffices); (ii) $u_{j+1}\ge p\,u_j$ for every cyclic $p^n$-extension of $k((x))$, which gives the lower bound for all faithful curves. For $n\le2$ and $(p,n)=(2,3)$, (i) is verified by hand (Theorem~\ref{thm:B}, Appendix~\ref{app:genus}). Nothing else in the proof of the Reichstein--Vistoli bound or of its sharpness uses ramification formulas.

label: lem:versal
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:versal}
Let $\tau\colon T=\operatorname{Spec} P\to\operatorname{Spec} F$ be a $G$-torsor over a field $F\supseteq k$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item There is $x\inW_n(P)$ with $g(x)-x=1$, and for any such $x$ the twist ${}^{\tau}\!W_n$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{A}^n_F$: its coordinate ring is $F[h_0,\dots,h_{n-1}]$, where $h=z-x\inW_n(P\otimes_kk[W_n])$. On points: for a field $F'\supseteq F$, an $F'$-point of ${}^{\tau}\!W_n$ is a $G$-equivariant morphism $T_{F'}\toW_n$, i.e.\ an element $y\inW_n(P\otimes_FF')$ with $g(y)-y=1$, and it corresponds to $h=y-x\inW_n(F')=F'^{\,n}$. For $\tau=\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ one may take $x=z$, so that $h=y-z$.
\item $W_n$ is $\tau$-versal for every $G$-torsor $\tau$ over every field $F\supseteq k$.
\item $\operatorname{ed}_k(G)=\operatorname{ed}_k(W_n)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le n$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) By Artin--Schreier--Witt theory (Section~\ref{ss:witt}) $\tau\cong\tau_a$ for some $a\inW_n(F)$, so $P$ contains $x'\inW_n(P)$ with $g(x')=x'+1$; put $x=x'$. Since $W_n$ is affine, ${}^{\tau}\!W_n=\operatorname{Spec} R$ with $R=(P\otimes_kk[W_n])^G=P[z_0,\dots,z_{n-1}]^G$, $G$ acting diagonally. In $W_n(P[z])$ put $h:=z-x$. As $G$ acts on $P[z]$ by ring automorphisms, it acts on $W_n(P[z])$ by ring automorphisms, and $g(h)=(z+1)-(x+1)=h$; so the coordinates $h_0,\dots,h_{n-1}$ lie in $R$. Since Witt addition and subtraction are given by polynomials with integer coefficients, of the form $(a\pm b)_i=a_i\pm b_i+(\text{polynomial in }a_0,\dots,a_{i-1},b_0,\dots,b_{i-1})$, we have $z_i=h_i+(\text{polynomial in }h_0,\dots,h_{i-1},x_0,\dots,x_i)$ and $h_i=z_i+(\text{polynomial in }z_0,\dots,z_{i-1},x_0,\dots,x_i)$. Hence $P[z]=P[h_0,\dots,h_{n-1}]$ with $h_0,\dots,h_{n-1}$ algebraically independent over $P$, i.e.\ $P[z]=P\otimes_FF[h]$, and $G$ acts on it through the factor $P$ only. Choosing an $F$-basis of $F[h]$ shows $(P\otimes_FF[h])^G=P^G\otimes_FF[h]=F[h]$. So $R=F[h_0,\dots,h_{n-1}]$ and ${}^{\tau}\!W_n\cong\mathbb{A}^n_F$. An $F'$-point of $\operatorname{Spec} R$ is the specialisation $h\mapsto h(y)\in F'^{\,n}$; via $P[z]=P\otimes_FF[h]$ it corresponds to the $G$-equivariant $P$-algebra map $P[z]\to P\otimes_FF'$, i.e.\ to the equivariant morphism $T_{F'}\toW_n$ with $y=x+h$, which is the identification of Fact~[A,\,\ref{A-fact:rs}](a). For $\tau=\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$, $P=L$ and $x=z\inW_n(L)$ satisfies $g(x)-x=\varepsilon$.

(b) Let $U\subseteqW_n$ be a dense $G$-invariant open subset. Then ${}^{\tau}\!U$ is a nonempty open subscheme of ${}^{\tau}\!W_n\cong\mathbb{A}^n_F$ \cite[Cor.~3.4]{DR15}, and $F\supseteq k$ is infinite, so ${}^{\tau}\!U(F)\ne\emptyset$, and $U$ is $\tau$-weakly versal by Fact~[A,\,\ref{A-fact:rs}](a).

(c) $G$ acts freely on the irreducible variety $W_n$, so $W_n$ is generically free and primitive, and by (b) and Fact~[A,\,\ref{A-fact:rs}](c), $\operatorname{ed}_k(W_n)\ge\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)$ for every $G$-torsor $\tau$ over every $F\supseteq k$, i.e.\ $\operatorname{ed}_k(W_n)\ge\operatorname{ed}_k(G)$. By the identity $\operatorname{ed}_k(Y)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_Y)$ of \cite[Section~\ref{A-ss:ed}]{PA}, $\operatorname{ed}_k(W_n)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{W_n})=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})$, since the torsor $W_n\toW_n/G$ has generic fibre $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$; and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le\operatorname{ed}_k(G)$ by definition and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le\operatorname{trdeg}_kK=n$ (the bound $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^n)\le n$ is also in \cite{Ledet04}, and for trigonalizable group schemes in \cite[Thm.~1.4]{TV}).

label: cor:insep
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:insep}
For $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ over an algebraically closed $k$ of characteristic $p$, the profile only sees separable extensions: $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau)=\min\{\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F'):[F':F]\le d,\ F'/F\text{ separable}\}$, and every cyclic extension of degree $p$ of $F$ (for $p=2$: every separable quadratic extension) is an Artin--Schreier extension $F(v_f)$, $v_f^p-v_f=f\in F\smallsetminus\wp F$.

label: rem:insepwitt
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:insepwitt}
For $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ the isomorphism $\sigma_*(\tau\otimes F^{1/p^m})\cong\tau$ can be seen on Witt classes (Section~\ref{ss:witt}): if $a\inW_n(F)$ is the class of $\tau$, the class of $\tau\otimes F^{1/p^m}$ is $a$ viewed in $W_n(F^{1/p^m})$, and by functoriality of the Artin--Schreier--Witt isomorphism the class of $\sigma_*(\tau\otimes F^{1/p^m})$ is $W_n(\sigma)(a)=F^m(a)$. Since $F(a)-a=\wp(a)$, $F^m(a)\equiv a\bmod\wpW_n(F)$.

label: prop:intermediate
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:intermediate}
Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $p$, $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$, $K_j=L^{\langle g^{p^j}\rangle}$, $1\le j\le n-1$. Then $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes K_j$ is induced from the $\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-j}$-torsor $L/K_j$, which is the generic $\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-j}$-torsor over the base field $k':=k(z_0,\dots,z_{j-1})$, and
\[
\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes_KK_j)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-j})\le n-j .
\]
In particular $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes K_1)\ge\min(n-1,2)$, so for $n=3$ the subextension $K_1=K(z_0)$ is never a witness for $d_1=p$.
head: environment
name: the intermediate fields of $L/K$ for $G=\Z/p^n$

title: Proof
body_md:
$L\otimes_KK_j\cong\prod_{G/H}L$ with $H=\langle g^{p^j}\rangle$, i.e.\ $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes K_j=\operatorname{Ind}_H^G(L/K_j)$, and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes K_j)=\operatorname{ed}_k(L/K_j)$ by Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:ind}]. By \eqref{eq:gpj}, $H$ acts on $(z_j,\dots,z_{n-1})$ by the Witt translation of $W_{n-j}$ and fixes $z_0,\dots,z_{j-1}$, so $L/K_j$ is the $\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-j}$-torsor of class $s':=\wp_{W_{n-j}}(z_j,\dots,z_{n-1})\inW_{n-j}(K_j)$. Its coordinates satisfy $s'_i=z_{j+i}^p-z_{j+i}+(\text{polynomial in }z_j,\dots,z_{j+i-1})$, while $s_{j+i}=z_{j+i}^p-z_{j+i}+(\text{polynomial in }z_0,\dots,z_{j+i-1})$; hence $q_i:=s_{j+i}-s'_i$ is a polynomial in $z_0,\dots,z_{j+i-1}$, and it is $H$-invariant. Now $H$ fixes $z_0,\dots,z_{j-1}$ and, through the truncation $W_{n-j}\toW_i$, acts on $(z_j,\dots,z_{j+i-1})$ by the Witt translation of $W_i$, whose quotient map is the finite \'etale Galois map $\wp\colonW_i\toW_i$, $(z_j,\dots,z_{j+i-1})\mapsto(s'_0,\dots,s'_{i-1})$; as $\mathbb{A}^i$ is normal, $k[z_j,\dots,z_{j+i-1}]^H=k[s'_0,\dots,s'_{i-1}]$. Hence $q_i\in k[z_0,\dots,z_{j-1}][s'_0,\dots,s'_{i-1}]$. Consequently
\[
K_j=k'(s'_0,\dots,s'_{n-j-1}),\qquad k'=k(z_0,\dots,z_{j-1}),
\]
The $n$ elements $z_0,\dots,z_{j-1},s'_0,\dots,s'_{n-j-1}$ generate $K_j$, which has transcendence degree $n$ over $k$, so they are algebraically independent. Put $F'':=k(s'_0,\dots,s'_{n-j-1})$. Then $s'$ is the class of the generic $\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-j}$-torsor $\tau_{n-j}$ over $F''$, $K_j=F''(z_0,\dots,z_{j-1})$ is purely transcendental over $F''$, and $L/K_j=\tau_{n-j}\otimes_{F''}K_j$. By Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:constant}](i) and Lemma~\ref{lem:versal}(c), $\operatorname{ed}_k(L/K_j)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{n-j})=\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-j})\le n-j$.

label: lem:imageB
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:imageB}
Let $Z$ be an irreducible $G$-variety with faithful action, $\tau\colon T\to\operatorname{Spec} F$ a torsor with $T$ connected, and $f\colon T\to Z$ equivariant. Then the closure of $f(T)$ is an irreducible $G$-stable closed subset $Y$, and the point $f(T)$ is free iff no $1\ne h\in G$ acts trivially on $Y$; for $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ this holds iff $G$ acts faithfully on $Y$. If $\dim Z=1$, $G\ne1$ and $f(T)$ is free, then $f$ is dominant if $k$ is algebraically closed; for arbitrary $k$ it is dominant unless $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)=0$.
head: environment
name: image of a free point

title: Proof
body_md: As $T$ is connected and $Z$ separated, $f(T)$ is a single point $\xi$ (the image of the generic point of $T$), and $h\xi=\xi$ for all $h\in G$ by equivariance, so $Y=\overline{\{\xi\}}$ is $G$-stable and irreducible. For $h\ne1$, $\xi\in Z^h$ iff $Y\subseteq Z^h$ iff $h$ acts trivially on $Y$. For $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ all nontrivial subgroups contain $g^{p^{n-1}}$, so $\xi$ is free iff $g^{p^{n-1}}$ is nontrivial on $Y$ iff the action on $Y$ is faithful. If $k$ is algebraically closed, a $G$-stable closed point is fixed by $G$, hence not free when $G\ne1$; so for a curve a free point has $Y=Z$. For arbitrary $k$ the closed point $\xi=Y$ can be free (e.g.\ $k=\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{Z}/2$ acting on $\mathbb{P}^1$ by $z\mapsto-z$, $\xi=(z^2+1)$); then $\xi=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ is a $G$-torsor over the finite extension $\kappa^G$ of $k$, the equivariant map $T\to\xi$ identifies $\tau$ with the base change of $\xi\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa^G$ by (T2), and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)=0$.

label: def:DB
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:DB}
For a quasi-projective generically free primitive $G$-variety $Z$ and a torsor $\tau$ over $F$, let $D(Z,\tau)\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ be the set of degrees of closed points of ${}^{\tau}\!Z$ lying in the free locus, and $\delta_\mathrm{free}(Z,\tau):=\min D(Z,\tau)$ ($=\infty$ if empty). Write $D(Z)$, $\delta_\mathrm{free}(Z)$ for $\tau=\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$. For an affine curve $U$ with smooth projective model $\overline{U}$ such that $\overline{U}^{\mathrm{free}}=U$ we write $D(U)=D(\overline{U})$.

label: cor:jumpsB
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:jumpsB}
For every $G$-torsor $\tau$ and $0\le j\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)$,
\[
d_j(\tau)=\min\{\delta_\mathrm{free}(Z,\tau):Z\text{ quasi-projective generically free primitive},\ \dim Z\le j\}.
\]
For $k$ perfect, $j=1$ and $\tau$ with connected total space $T$ (e.g.\ $\tau=\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$) the minimum may be restricted to smooth projective irreducible curves with faithful $G$-action provided $d_1(\tau)$ is attained by an $F'$ with $T\times_FF'$ connected; and then the free point is dominant (Lemma~\ref{lem:imageB}, since $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')=1\ne0$). More precisely, for every finite $F'/F$ with $T\times_FF'$ connected and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes_FF')=1$ there is a smooth projective irreducible curve with faithful $G$-action whose twist by $\tau\otimes F'$ has a free, dominant $F'$-point. For $\tau=\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ with $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ this holds whenever $F'\not\supseteq K_1=K(z_0)$, in particular whenever $p\nmid[F':K]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The first statement is Theorem~[A,\,\ref{A-thm:geom}]. For the second (where $k$ is assumed perfect, so that the smooth projective model of an irreducible curve is a smooth curve over $k$), let $F'$ be as in the last sentence; by the proof of Theorem~[A,\,\ref{A-thm:geom}] ((1)$\Rightarrow$(3) with $m=1$, where $T_{F'}$ connected makes $Z$ irreducible with faithful action), there is an irreducible $Z$ with faithful $G$-action, $\dim Z\le1$, whose twist has a free $F'$-point, and $\dim Z=1$ since $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')=1$ (Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:freepoint}]). So $Z$ is an irreducible faithful $G$-curve, its smooth projective model $\tilde Z$ carries the induced action, the free $F'$-point of ${}^{\tau'}\!Z$ is dominant (Lemma~\ref{lem:imageB}, as $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')=1\ne0$) hence corresponds to a $G$-equivariant $T_{F'}\to\tilde Z$ whose image is the generic point, free because the action on $\tilde Z$ is faithful (an element acting trivially on the generic point acts trivially on $\tilde Z$); conversely a free point on $\tilde Z$ is dominant, so lands in the open $Z$. For $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ the intermediate fields of $L/K$ are the chain $K\subset K_1\subset\dots\subset L$, so a finite $F'/K$ has $F'\cap L=K$ (i.e.\ $L\otimes_KF'$ a field, $L/K$ being Galois) iff $F'\not\supseteq K_1$.

label: fact:rsd
title: Fact
body_md:
\label{fact:rsd}
If $F$ is a large field and $X$ a generically free $G$-variety with a smooth $G$-fixed $k$-point, then $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)\le\operatorname{ed}_k(X)\le\dim X$ for every $G$-torsor $\tau$ over $F$; and if $G$ is a finite $p$-group and $\operatorname{char}k=p$, then $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)\le1$ for every $G$-torsor over a large field \cite[Lemma~9.1]{RS22}.

label: lem:tower
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:tower}
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $p$, $a\inW_n(F)$ and $0\le r\le n$. There is a tower $F=F^{(0)}\subseteq F^{(1)}\subseteq\dots\subseteq F^{(n-r)}$ of Artin--Schreier extensions (each of degree $1$ or $p$), hence $[F^{(n-r)}:F]\le p^{n-r}$, such that
\[
a\equiv(a_0,\dots,a_{r-1},0,\dots,0)\bmod\wpW_n(F^{(n-r)}).
\]
The $i$-th layer is $F^{(i)}=F^{(i-1)}(v_i)$ with $v_i^p-v_i=b_i$, where $b_1=a_r$ and $b_i$ (for $i\ge2$) is the coordinate of index $r+i-1$ of the class obtained at the previous step; in general $b_i\ne a_{r+i-1}$ because of the Witt carries.
head: environment
name: truncation tower

title: Proof
body_md:
Induction on $n-r$; there is nothing to do if $r=n$. Let $r<n$. By \eqref{eq:Vsplit}, $a=(a_0,\dots,a_{r-1},0,\dots,0)+V^r(a')$ with $a'=(a_r,\dots,a_{n-1})\inW_{n-r}(F)$, and $a'=[a_r]+V(a'')$. Let $v^p-v=a_r$ in $F^{(1)}=F(v)$. In $W_{n-r}(F^{(1)})$ the vectors $[a_r]=[v^p-v]$ and $\wp[v]=[v^p]-[v]$ have the same coordinate of index $0$, so $[a_r]=\wp[v]+V(e)$ for some $e\inW_{n-r-1}(F^{(1)})$. Since $\wp$ commutes with $V^r$, $V^r\wp[v]\in\wpW_n(F^{(1)})$ and
\[
a\equiv(a_0,\dots,a_{r-1},0,\dots,0)+V^{r+1}(a''+e)=(a_0,\dots,a_{r-1},0,b_2,\dots,b_{n-r})\bmod\wpW_n(F^{(1)}),
\]
with $b_2,\dots$ the coordinates of $a''+e$ (again \eqref{eq:Vsplit}). Apply the induction hypothesis (with $r+1$) to this vector over $F^{(1)}$.

label: prop:trunc
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:trunc}
For $0\le j\le n$: $\operatorname{ed}^{[p^j]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le n-j$. In particular $d_{n-1}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le p$, $d_1(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le p^{n-1}$, $d_0(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le p^n$. More generally, for every $G$-torsor $\tau_a$ over a field $F\supseteq k$ one has $\operatorname{ed}^{[p^j]}_k(\tau_a)\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{(a_0,\dots,a_{n-j-1},0,\dots,0)})\le\operatorname{trdeg}_kk(a_0,\dots,a_{n-j-1})$.

name: truncation bound

title: Proof
body_md: Lemma~\ref{lem:tower} with $r=n-j$: over $F^{(j)}$, of degree $\le p^j$, the class is $(a_0,\dots,a_{n-j-1},0,\dots,0)$, a Witt vector with coordinates in $k(a_0,\dots,a_{n-j-1})$, so the torsor descends to that field. For $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$, $\operatorname{trdeg}_kk(s_0,\dots,s_{n-j-1})=n-j$.

label: lem:lift
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:lift}
Let $F\supseteq k$ be a field, $n\ge2$, $a\inW_n(F)$, and $\bar a\inW_{n-1}(F)$ its truncation, the class of the $\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-1}$-torsor $\tau_{\bar a}$ induced by $\mathbb{Z}/p^n\to\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-1}$. For every field extension $F'/F$,
\[
\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_a\otimes F')\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\bar a}\otimes F')+1 .
\]
Consequently $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_a)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\bar a})+1$ and $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]'}_k(\tau_a)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[d]'}_k(\tau_{\bar a})+1$ for every $d\ge1$. For the generic torsors $\tau_n$ over $K=k(s_0,\dots,s_{n-1})$ and $\tau_{n-1}$ over $k(s_0,\dots,s_{n-2})$ this gives $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_n)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{n-1})+1$ and $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]'}_k(\tau_n)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[d]'}_k(\tau_{n-1})+1$, hence
\[
d_{j+1}(\tau_n)\le d_j(\tau_{n-1}),\qquad d_{j+1}^{(p')}(\tau_n)\le d_j^{(p')}(\tau_{n-1})\qquad(0\le j\le n-1).
\]
head: environment
name: lifting one Witt layer

title: Proof
body_md: Let $e=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\bar a}\otimes F')$: there are a field $k\subseteq F_0\subseteq F'$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_kF_0=e$, $b\inW_{n-1}(F_0)$ and $y\inW_{n-1}(F')$ with $\bar a=b+\wp y$. Let $\tilde y=(y,0)\inW_n(F')$. Truncation $W_n\toW_{n-1}$ is a ring map commuting with $\wp$, so $a-\wp\tilde y$ has truncation $b$, i.e.\ $a-\wp\tilde y=(b_0,\dots,b_{n-2},c)$ for some $c\in F'$. This vector lies in $W_n(F_0(c))$ and $\operatorname{trdeg}_kF_0(c)\le e+1$, so $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_a\otimes F')\le e+1$. Taking the minimum over $F'/F$ of degree $\le d$ (and prime to $p$) gives the statements on profiles. For the generic torsors, the truncation of $\tau_n$ is $\tau_{n-1}\otimes K$, and an extension $F'_0$ of degree $d$ of $k(s_0,\dots,s_{n-2})$ gives the extension $F'_0\otimes K=F'_0(s_{n-1})$ of $K$ of the same degree, over which a descent of $\tau_{n-1}\otimes F'_0$ remains a descent; so $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{n-1}\otimes K)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{n-1})$, and likewise for the prime-to-$p$ profiles. The inequalities for the jump degrees follow.

label: rem:lift
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:lift}
(i) At $(2,3)$, Lemma~\ref{lem:lift} with $j=1$ and Theorem~\ref{thm:n2}(d) give $d_2^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le d_1^{(p')}(\tau_2)=3$; this is the upper bound in Theorem~\ref{thm:23main}(d), made explicit there. With $j=0$ it gives $d_1(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le d_0(\tau_2)=4$, the bound of Proposition~\ref{prop:trunc}.
(ii) At $(3,3)$ it gives $d_2^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le d_1^{(p')}(\tau_2)\le p^2-p+1=7$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:n2p}); as the prime-to-$p$ profile can only change at degrees prime to $3$, $d_2^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le7$.
(iii) The lemma does not interact with Ledet's conjecture: it bounds $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_n)$ by $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{n-1})+1$, which is the bound $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^n)\le n$ again.

label: prop:S0
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:S0}
Let $n\ge2$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $S_0$ is an irreducible $G$-stable hypersurface of dimension $n-1$ on which $G$ acts freely. Under the identification ${}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!W_n\cong\mathbb{A}^n_K$, $y\mapsto h=y-z$, of Lemma~\ref{lem:versal},
\[
{}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!S_0=\{h\in\mathbb{A}^n_K:(s+\wp h)_{n-1}=0\}.
\]
\item ${}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!S_0$ has a free closed point of degree $p$, namely $h=(0,\dots,0,v)$ with $v^p-v=-s_{n-1}$, and it has no $K$-point unless $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le n-1$. Hence $d_{n-1}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=\min_Z\delta_\mathrm{free}(Z)\le p$, the minimum taken over quasi-projective generically free primitive $G$-varieties $Z$ of dimension $\le n-1$; at $p=2$ this minimum is $1$ if $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/2^n)\le n-1$ and $2$ otherwise.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) $S_0$ is $G$-stable because $\wp$ is $G$-invariant. The restriction of the $G$-torsor $\wp\colonW_n\toW_n$ to the hyperplane $\{s_{n-1}=0\}\cong\mathbb{A}^{n-1}$ is a $G$-torsor $S_0\to\mathbb{A}^{n-1}$ whose generic fibre is the Artin--Schreier--Witt torsor of class $a:=(s_0,\dots,s_{n-2},0)\inW_n(K_{(n-1)})$, $K_{(n-1)}=k(s_0,\dots,s_{n-2})$. So $S_0$ has dimension $n-1$, $G$ acts freely on it, and it is irreducible iff this generic fibre is a field, i.e.\ iff $a$ has order $p^n$ in $W_n(K_{(n-1)})/\wp$. Now $p^{n-1}a=V^{n-1}F^{n-1}a=(0,\dots,0,s_0^{p^{n-1}})$, which by \eqref{eq:Vker} is $\equiv0$ iff $s_0^{p^{n-1}}\equiv s_0$ lies in $\wp K_{(n-1)}$; this fails, since over $k(s_1,\dots,s_{n-2})$ the element $s_0$ has a simple pole at $s_0=\infty$, whereas an element $w^p-w$ has a pole of order divisible by $p$ there or none. By Lemma~\ref{lem:versal}(a), a $K'$-point of ${}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!W_n$ ($K'\supseteq K$) is a $y\inW_n(L\otimes_KK')$ with $g(y)-y=1$, and $h:=y-z$ is then $G$-invariant, i.e.\ $h\inW_n(K')$; the point lies in ${}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!S_0$ iff $(\wp(z+h))_{n-1}=(s+\wp h)_{n-1}=0$.

(b) By \eqref{eq:Vsplit} and $\wp V^{n-1}=V^{n-1}\wp$: $s+\wp V^{n-1}(v)=s+V^{n-1}(v^p-v)=(s_0,\dots,s_{n-2},0)$. The residue field $K(v)$ has degree $p$, because $-s_{n-1}\notin\wp K$ (simple pole at $s_{n-1}=\infty$). As $G$ acts freely on $S_0$, every point of ${}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!S_0$ is free. A free $K$-point on the $(n-1)$-dimensional $S_0$ gives $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le n-1$ by Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:freepoint}]. The formula $d_{n-1}=\min_Z\delta_\mathrm{free}(Z)$ is Corollary~\ref{cor:jumpsB}, and the point of degree $p$ gives $\le p$; at $p=2$, $d_{n-1}=1$ iff $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le n-1$.

title: Remark
body_md: By Proposition~\ref{prop:S0}(b), the minimum over all $G$-varieties of dimension $\le n-1$ of the degree of a free point on the twist equals $d_{n-1}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le p$: it carries at most one bit when $p=2$. Graded information on the profile therefore has to come from the degree of the base change, via curves (Section~\ref{ss:rigid}), or from varieties one at a time (the sets $D(Z)$, Proposition~\ref{prop:DX}).

label: fact:pic
title: Fact
body_md:
\label{fact:pic}
Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$ of genus $g(C)$, and $D$ a divisor on $C$; $\mathcal L(D)=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C(D))$, $\ell(D)=\dim_k\mathcal L(D)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ is represented by a $k$-group scheme whose components $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$ are torsors under the Jacobian $J=\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$, an abelian variety of dimension $g(C)$; since $C(k)\ne\emptyset$, $\operatorname{Pic}(C_F)=\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(F)$ for every field $F\supseteq k$, compatibly with degrees and with pullback by automorphisms of $C$ \cite[8.1, Prop.~4; 8.2, Thm.~3; 8.4, Thm.~3]{BLR90}, \cite[Thm.~9.2.5]{Kl05}; $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is an abelian variety of dimension $g(C)$ by \cite[8.4, Thm.~1]{BLR90}.
\item For a field $F\supseteq k$: $\mathcal L(D_F)=\mathcal L(D)\otimes_kF$ (flat base change), so $\ell(D_F)=\ell(D)$.
\item (Riemann--Roch) $\ell(D)-\ell(K_C-D)=\deg D+1-g(C)$ \cite[IV.1.3]{Hart77}. If $g(C)\ge1$ and $\deg D\ge1$ then $\ell(D)\le\deg D$ \cite[IV, Ex.~1.5]{Hart77}; if $g(C)=1$ and $\deg D\ge1$ then $\ell(D)=\deg D$.
\item (Clifford) If $D$ is effective and special ($\ell(K_C-D)>0$) then $\ell(D)-1\le\frac12\deg D$ \cite[IV.5.4]{Hart77}.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: curves and Picard schemes

label: lem:curvesB
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:curvesB}
\textup{(i)} $\operatorname{PGL}_2(\bar k)$ has no element of order $p^2$ if $\operatorname{char}k=p$; in particular $\operatorname{PGL}_2(k)$ has none. \textup{(ii)} Let $p=2$ and $E$ a supersingular elliptic curve over $k$ algebraically closed. Then $\operatorname{Aut}(E)$ (all automorphisms of the curve) has no element of order $8$. \textup{(iii)} An irreducible curve dominated by $\mathbb{A}^m_k$ has smooth projective model $\mathbb{P}^1$. \textup{(iv)} A nonconstant morphism of smooth projective curves $E\to C$ over a perfect field satisfies $g(C)\le g(E)$.
head: environment
name: two facts on curves

title: Proof
body_md: (i) A $p$-element of $\operatorname{PGL}_2(\bar k)$ lifts to $A\in\mathrm{GL}_2(\bar k)$ with $A^{p^m}=1$ after scaling, so $(A-1)^{p^m}=0$, $A=1+N$ with $N^2=0$, and $A^p=1+pN=1$. (ii) $\operatorname{Aut}(E)=E(k)\rtimes\operatorname{Aut}(E,O)$, and $\operatorname{Aut}(E,O)$ is a group of order $24$ with Sylow $2$-subgroup $Q_8$ \cite[Thm.~III.10.1 and App.~A, Prop.~1.2]{Silverman09}, so its elements of $2$-power order have order $\le4$. Let $\phi=t_P\circ\alpha$ with $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(E,O)$, $t_P$ translation by $P$, and $\phi^8=1$; then $\alpha^8=1$, so $m:=\operatorname{ord}\alpha\in\{1,2,4\}$. If $m=1$, $\operatorname{ord}\phi=\operatorname{ord} P$, which is odd because $E(k)[2]=0$ for a supersingular curve in characteristic $2$. If $m\in\{2,4\}$: $\phi^m=t_Q$ with $Q=(1+\alpha+\dots+\alpha^{m-1})P$, and $(\alpha-1)(1+\alpha+\dots+\alpha^{m-1})=\alpha^m-1=0$ in the domain $\mathrm{End}(E)$ with $\alpha-1\ne0$, so $Q=0$ and $\operatorname{ord}\phi\mid m\le4$. (iii) is L\"uroth's theorem, valid in every characteristic (restrict the dominant map to the curve $t\mapsto(t,t^N,t^{N^2},\dots,t^{N^{m-1}})$ with $N$ large, which is not contained in a fibre, to get a nonconstant $\mathbb{A}^1\to C$). (iv) Factor $E\to C$ as a purely inseparable map (a power of Frobenius composed with an isomorphism, genus preserving) followed by a separable map, to which Riemann--Hurwitz applies.

label: lem:twistL
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: the twist is trivialised by $L$

title: Proof
body_md: Write $T=\operatorname{Spec} L$. Since $L/K$ is Galois with group $G$, $T\times_KT\cong G\times T$ via $(t_1,t_2)\mapsto(\gamma,t_2)$ with $t_1=\gamma t_2$. Hence $X\times_KT=((T\times_kC)/G)\times_KT=(T\times_KT\times_kC)/G\cong(G\times T\times_kC)/G\cong T\times_kC$, the quotient being by the diagonal action on the first and last factors (the twist commutes with base change, \cite[\S3]{DR15}). For (a), the automorphism $\operatorname{id}_X\times\operatorname{Spec}(h)$ of $X\times_KT$ acts on the second tensor factor $T$ only. Under $T\times_KT\cong G\times T$, $(t_1,t_2)\mapsto(\gamma,t_2)$ with $t_1=\gamma t_2$, replacing $t_2$ by $ht_2$ changes $\gamma$ to $\gamma h^{-1}$ (as $t_1=\gamma h^{-1}(ht_2)$). On $(G\times T\times_kC)/G$ the class of $(\gamma,t,c)$ is therefore sent to that of $(\gamma h^{-1},ht,c)=(\gamma,ht,hc)$, using the diagonal $G$-action; this is $h_C\times\operatorname{Spec}(h)$ on $T\times_kC$ under the last identification, which is $\phi_h$. For (b), an $F'$-point of $X$ is by Fact~[A,\,\ref{A-fact:rs}](a) a $G$-equivariant $x\colon T_{F'}\to C$, and its base change to $T$ is, under the displayed isomorphism, the section $(x,\operatorname{id})$ of $T_{F'}\times_kC\to T_{F'}$; its first component is $x$.

label: setup:witness
title: Setup
body_md:
\label{setup:witness}
This is the setting of [A,\,\ref{A-prop:witness}]; nothing in it, in Lemma~\ref{lem:twistL}, or in parts (b),(c) of Proposition~\ref{prop:rigid} uses that $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ or that the characteristic is $p$: it holds for any finite group $G$ and any $G$-Galois extension $L/K$ with $L$ purely transcendental over $k$, with $\tau=\operatorname{Spec} L$. We write it in the notation of this paper, with $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}=\operatorname{Spec} L$. Let $F'/K$ be a finite field extension of degree $d$ such that $L\otimes_KF'$ is a field and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes_KF')\le1$. By [A,\,\S\ref{A-ss:ed},\,(B3)], $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes F')=1$ (a torsor whose total space is a field is not split), so by Theorem~[A,\,\ref{A-thm:geom}] and Corollary~\ref{cor:jumpsB} there are a smooth projective curve $C$ over $k$ with a faithful $G$-action and a free point $P\in{}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!C(F')$; the attached equivariant morphism $x\colon\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_KF')\to C$ is dominant (Lemma~\ref{lem:imageB}). Let $\xi$ be the closed point of $X={}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!C$ underlying $P$, of degree $e=[\kappa(\xi):K]$, which divides $d$ as $\kappa(\xi)\subseteq F'$. Put
\[
D_P:=\tfrac de\,\xi\quad(\text{an effective $K$-rational divisor of degree }d\text{ on }X),\qquad \Delta:=\psi(D_P\otimes_KL)\ \text{on }C_L .
\]
Since $\kappa(\xi)\otimes_KL\subseteq F'\otimes_KL$ is a field, $\xi\otimes_KL$ is a single closed point $\eta$ of $X_L$, and $\Delta=\frac de\,\psi(\eta)$.

label: prop:rigid
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:rigid}
In Setup~\ref{setup:witness}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $g(C)\ge1$.
\item There is an effective divisor $D_0$ on $C$ of degree $d$ with $\Delta\sim D_0\otimes_kL$ on $C_L$ and $h^*D_0\sim D_0$ for every $h\in G$.
\item $\ell(D_0)\ge2$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: rigidity lemma

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) If $C\cong\mathbb{P}^1$ then $G\cong\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ embeds in $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{P}^1)=\operatorname{PGL}_2(k)$, which has no element of order $p^2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:curvesB}(i)); as $n\ge2$ this is impossible.

(b) By Fact~\ref{fact:pic}(a) the class of $\Delta$ is an $L$-point of $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$, a torsor under $J$; as $k$ is algebraically closed it has a $k$-point and is isomorphic to $J$ as a $k$-variety. Since $L=k(z_0,\dots,z_{n-1})$ is purely transcendental over $k$, Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:constant}](ii), applied to the abelian variety $J$, gives $J(L)=J(k)$; so $[\Delta]$ is the image of a class $c_0\in\operatorname{Pic}^d(C)$. As $\Delta$ is effective, $\ell(c_0\otimes L)\ge1$, hence $\ell(c_0)\ge1$ by Fact~\ref{fact:pic}(b), and we may choose $D_0\in c_0$ effective. The divisor $D_P\otimes_KL$ is invariant under $\operatorname{id}\times\operatorname{Spec}(g)$, so by Lemma~\ref{lem:twistL}(a) $\phi_g(\Delta)=\Delta$. Since $D_0$ is defined over $k$, $\phi_g^*(D_0\otimes L)=(g^*D_0)\otimes L$; hence $(g^*D_0)\otimes L\sim\Delta\sim D_0\otimes L$, and as $\operatorname{Pic}(C)=\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(k)\to\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(L)$ is injective, $g^*D_0\sim D_0$. Iterate for the powers of $g$.

(c) Suppose $\ell(D_0)=1$. Then $\ell(D_0\otimes L)=1$ by Fact~\ref{fact:pic}(b), so $D_0\otimes L$ is the only effective divisor in its class, and $\Delta=D_0\otimes L$. Thus $\psi(\eta)$ lies over a point of the finite set $\operatorname{Supp}(D_0)\subseteq C(k)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:twistL}(b), $x$ factors through $\operatorname{Spec}(F'\otimes_KL)\to\eta\to X_L\xrightarrow{\psi}C_L\to C$, so its image is a closed point of $C$, contradicting the dominance of $x$.

label: rem:rigid-d1
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:rigid-d1}
For $d=1$ the proposition reproves $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^n)\ge2$ for $n\ge2$: by (a) and Fact~\ref{fact:pic}(c), $\ell(D_0)\le\deg D_0=1$, against (c). The same argument at $n=2$ is Proposition~\ref{prop:G1}. The only property of $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ used is that $L$ is purely transcendental over $k$; the only property of $G$ used is that it is cyclic of order $p^n$ with $n\ge2$ (through Lemma~\ref{lem:curvesB}(i)). In particular nothing about the Witt coordinates of the class $s$ enters.

title: Remark
body_md: Parts (b) and (c) are the general case of [A,\,\ref{A-lem:AJ}] and [A,\,\ref{A-prop:witness}], where the same constancy statement is proved by an embedding-theoretic argument; we use the twist formulation here because Step~2 of Theorem~\ref{thm:ptp} needs that $\Delta$ is supported on a single closed point of $C_L$ of degree $e\ge2$ over $L$. label: prop:rigidN
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:rigidN}
Let $m\ge2$, let $H\cong\mathbb{Z}/p^m$ act faithfully on a smooth projective curve $C$ over $k$, and let $D_0$ be an effective divisor on $C$ with $\ell:=\ell(D_0)\ge2$ and $h^*D_0\sim D_0$ for all $h\in H$. Then $\deg D_0\ge p^{m-1}$.
head: environment
name: rigidity lemma, $\PGL_\ell$ form

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $B$ be the base locus of $|D_0|$ and $D_1=D_0-B$, $e'=\deg D_1\le\deg D_0$, $\mathcal L=\mathcal L(D_1)=\mathcal L(D_0)$, so $\dim\mathcal L=\ell$. For $h\in H$, $h^*$ preserves $|D_0|$, hence $h^*B=B$ and $h^*D_1=D_1+\operatorname{div}(\varphi_h)$ with $\varphi_h\in k(C)^\times$. Then $A_h\colon f\mapsto\varphi_hh^*f$ is a linear automorphism of $\mathcal L$, well defined up to a scalar; this gives a homomorphism $\rho\colon H\to\operatorname{PGL}(\mathcal L)=\operatorname{PGL}_\ell(k)$ ($H$ is abelian, so the contravariance of $h\mapsto h^*$ is harmless).

The image. Let $a=\lceil\log_p\ell\rceil$, so $p^{a-1}<\ell\le p^a$. If $\rho(h)$ has order $p^r$, lift it to $A\in\operatorname{GL}(\mathcal L)$ with $A^{p^r}=\lambda\cdot\operatorname{id}$ and choose $\mu\in k$ with $\mu^{p^r}=\lambda$ ($k$ algebraically closed). Then $B_1=\mu^{-1}A$ satisfies $B_1^{p^r}=\operatorname{id}$, so $(B_1-1)^{p^r}=0$ in characteristic $p$ and $B_1$ is unipotent; hence $(B_1-1)^\ell=0$ and $B_1^{p^a}=1+(B_1-1)^{p^a}=1$. So the cyclic group $\rho(H)$ has order $\le p^a$, and $H_0:=\ker\rho$ has $|H_0|\ge\max(1,p^{m-a})$.

The kernel. Let $f_0,\dots,f_{\ell-1}$ be a basis of $\mathcal L$. Elements of $H_0$ act on $\mathcal L$ as scalars up to the factor $\varphi_h$, so they fix every ratio $f_i/f_0$; thus $H_0$ fixes pointwise the subfield $k(\Gamma)\subseteq k(C)$ generated by these ratios, where $\varphi\colon C\to\Gamma\subseteq\mathbb{P}^{\ell-1}$ is the morphism defined by the base-point-free system $|D_1|$. Let $\nu\colon\tilde\Gamma\to\Gamma$ be the normalisation and $E=\nu^*\mathcal O(1)$ (so $\deg E=\deg\Gamma$); $\varphi$ factors as $C\xrightarrow{\varphi'}\tilde\Gamma$ of degree $\delta=[k(C):k(\Gamma)]$ and $D_1\sim\varphi'^*E$, whence $e'=\delta\deg E$. The $\ell$ coordinate sections are linearly independent in $H^0(\tilde\Gamma,\mathcal O(E))$ since $\Gamma$ is non-degenerate, so $\ell\le\ell(E)\le\deg E+1$ (Fact~\ref{fact:pic}(c) and its genus-$0$ analogue). Since $\ell\ge2$ we have $\deg E\ge1$ (as $\ell(E)\ge\ell\ge2$). As $H_0$ acts faithfully on $k(C)$ and fixes $k(\Gamma)$, Artin's theorem gives $|H_0|=[k(C):k(C)^{H_0}]$, which divides $\delta=[k(C):k(\Gamma)]$. Therefore
\[
e'=\delta\deg E\ \ge\ |H_0|(\ell-1)\ \ge\ \max(1,p^{m-a})\,p^{a-1}\ \ge\ p^{m-1}
\]
(for $m\ge a$ this is $p^{m-a}p^{a-1}$; for $m<a$ it is $\ell-1\ge p^{a-1}\ge p^m$). Hence $\deg D_0\ge e'\ge p^{m-1}$.

label: thm:N1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:N1}
Let $n\ge2$ and let $F'/K$ be a finite field extension with $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes_KF')\le1$. Then $[F':K]\ge p^{n-1}$. Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ge2$ for every $d<p^{n-1}$; with Proposition~\ref{prop:trunc}, $d_1(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=p^{n-1}$ for all $p$ and all $n\ge2$.
\item $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ge p^{n-1}+1$.
\item $\operatorname{ed}^{[p^j]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=n-j$ for $j=n-2$ \textup{(}all $n\ge2$\textup{)}; in particular for $j=1$ and $n=3$, for every $p$.
\item $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_3)=1$ for $p^2\le d<p^3$ and $=2$ for $p\le d<p^2$, and $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_3)\in\{2,3\}$ for $d<p$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: the first jump degree of $\Z/p^n$

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:pi}] we may replace $F'$ by its separable closure of $K$, which only decreases the degree. So let $F'/K$ be separable. Choose an embedding of $F'$ into an algebraic closure containing $L$ and let $N_0=LF'$, $H=\operatorname{Gal}(N_0/F')\subseteq G$. The intermediate fields of $L/K$ are the $K_i=L^{\langle g^{p^i}\rangle}$, so $H=\langle g^{p^i}\rangle$ for some $0\le i\le n$, $L\cap F'=K_i$, $F'\supseteq K_i$ and $[F':K]=p^i[F':K_i]$. If $i\ge n-1$ then $[F':K]\ge p^{n-1}$ and we are done. Let $i\le n-2$, $m=n-i\ge2$, so $H\cong\mathbb{Z}/p^m$.

Now $L\otimes_KF'=\prod_{G/H}N_0$ with $N_0=L\otimes_{K_i}F'$ a field, and $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes F'=\operatorname{Ind}_H^G(N_0/F')$, where $N_0/F'$ is the base change of the $H$-torsor $L/K_i$. By Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:ind}], $\operatorname{ed}_k(N_0/F')=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes F')\le1$, and it equals $1$ because $N_0$ is a field. The statements of Setup~\ref{setup:witness}, Lemma~\ref{lem:twistL} and Proposition~\ref{prop:rigid}(b),(c) use only that the torsor is a Galois extension $L/K_i$ with cyclic group $H\cong\mathbb{Z}/p^m$ acting faithfully and that $L$ is purely transcendental over $k$ \textup{(}the genus statement~\textup{(a)} is not needed\textup{)}. So they apply with $(H,K_i,F')$ in place of $(G,K,F')$ and give a smooth projective curve $C$ with a faithful $H$-action and an effective divisor $D_0$ of degree $d'':=[F':K_i]$ with $\ell(D_0)\ge2$ and $h^*D_0\sim D_0$ for all $h\in H$. Proposition~\ref{prop:rigidN} gives $d''\ge p^{m-1}$, hence $[F':K]=p^id''\ge p^{n-1}$.

(a) follows from this and Proposition~\ref{prop:trunc} ($\operatorname{ed}^{[p^{n-1}]}\le1$). (b): a degree prime to $p$ is not $p^{n-1}$ for $n\ge2$. (c): $\operatorname{ed}^{[p^{n-2}]}\le2$ is Proposition~\ref{prop:trunc} and $\ge2$ is~(a). (d): the slots with $d\ge p^2$ and $p\le d<p^2$ are Proposition~\ref{prop:trunc}, Proposition~[A,\,\ref{A-prop:d0}] and (a); for $d<p$, $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^3)\le3$ and (a) gives $\ge2$.

label: cor:curvepts
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:curvepts}
Let $n\ge2$ and let $C$ be a smooth projective curve with a faithful $\mathbb{Z}/p^n$-action. Every closed point of the free locus of ${}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!C$ has degree $\ge p^{n-1}$; that is, $D(C)\cap[1,p^{n-1}-1]=\emptyset$ (Definition~\ref{def:DB}).
head: environment
name: free points on faithful curves

title: Proof
body_md: A free closed point $\xi$ of degree $e$ has residue field $F'=\kappa(\xi)$ with $[F':K]=e$, and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes F')\le1$ by Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:freepoint}]. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:N1}.

label: rem:N1sharp
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:N1sharp}
The bound is sharp: $\operatorname{ed}^{[p^{n-1}]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le1$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:trunc}. For example at $(2,2)$, $\operatorname{ed}^{[2]}_k(\tau_2)=1$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:n2}); at $(3,2)$, $\operatorname{ed}^{[3]}_k(\tau_2)=1$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:n2p}); and at $(2,3)$, $d_1(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=4$ (Section~\ref{sec:p2n3}). Theorem~\ref{thm:N1} concerns extensions of degree $<p^{n-1}$; the prime-to-$p$ degrees above $p^{n-1}$ are treated in Theorem~\ref{thm:ptp}, which gives $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=l_n(p)$. Which slots remain open, and how they relate to Ledet's conjecture, is discussed in Remark~\ref{rem:N1ledet}.

label: prop:tail
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:tail}
Let $G$ be a finite $p$-group and $\tau$ a $G$-torsor over a field $F\supseteq k$. Recall the prime-to-$p$ profile $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]'}_k(\tau)=\min\{\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F'):[F':F]\le d,\ p\nmid[F':F]\}$ (Definition~[A,\,\ref{A-def:profile}]), so that $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k\le\operatorname{ed}^{[d]'}_k$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $\operatorname{ed}_{k,p}(\tau)=\min_d\operatorname{ed}^{[d]'}_k(\tau)$, and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')\ge\operatorname{ed}_{k,p}(\tau)$ for every finite extension $F'/F$ of degree prime to $p$. Thus $\operatorname{ed}_{k,p}(\tau)$ is the terminal value of the prime-to-$p$ profile, and $\min_{p\nmid d}\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau)\le\operatorname{ed}_{k,p}(\tau)$.
\item $\operatorname{ed}_{k,p}(\tau)\le1$; hence $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]'}_k(\tau)\le1$ for all large $d$, i.e.\ $d_1^{(p')}(\tau)<\infty$. If $G\ne1$ and $\tau=\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$, the prime-to-$p$ profile never reaches $0$, so $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]'}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=1$ for every $d\ge d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})$.

label: lem:ASlayer
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:ASlayer}
Let $C\to C'$ be a Galois cover of smooth projective curves over $k$ with group $\langle\sigma\rangle\cong\mathbb{Z}/p$, totally ramified at $\infty\in C$ over $\infty'\in C'$, with lower break $l$ at $\infty$ (so $l\ge1$), and let $\hat F$ be the completion of $k(C)$ at $\infty$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item For every $x\in\hat F^\times$ with $p\nmid v_\infty(x)$: $v_\infty(\sigma x-x)=v_\infty(x)+l$.
\item Let $k(C)=k(C')(y)$ with $y^p-y=c\in k(C')$ and $v_{\infty'}(c)=-M<0$. Then $l\le M$, with equality iff $p\nmid M$. In particular $l$ is prime to $p$.
\item If $C\to C'$ is \'etale away from $\infty$, then $2g(C)-2=p\,(2g(C')-2)+(p-1)(l+1)$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Proof

e0$. Then $\sigma u-u=\sum_{j\ge1}a_j\pi^j((1+\varepsilon)^j-1)$ has valuation $\ge l+1$, so $\sigma u/u=1+\delta$ with $v(\delta)\ge l+1$; and $(1+\varepsilon)^r=1+r\varepsilon+\varepsilon^2(\dots)$ with $v(r\varepsilon)=l$ because $p
mid r$, and $v(\varepsilon^2)=2l>l$. Hence $\sigma x/x=(1+\delta)(1+\varepsilon)^r=1+r\varepsilon+(	ext{terms of valuation}>l)$, so $v(\sigma x-x)=v(x)+l$.

(b) The roots of $Y^p-Y-c$ in $k(C)$ are $y+\mathbb{F}_p$, and $\sigma y
e y$, so $\sigma y-y=j\in\mathbb{F}_p^	imes$. Suppose first $p

In the completion $\hat F'=k((\pi'))$ of $k(C')$ at $\infty'$ reduce $c$: while $c=\gamma\pi'^{-pa}+(	ext{higher terms})$ with $a>0$, replace $c$ by $c-\wp(\gamma^{1/p}\pi'^{-a})$, which has larger valuation. label: lem:lnformula
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) The completion at $\infty$ of $\overline{U}_n\to\mathbb{P}^1_t$ is the Artin--Schreier--Witt extension of $k((1/t))$ of class $[t]$, a reduced Witt vector whose only nonzero coordinate has a pole of order $1$. By the formula for the upper breaks of Artin--Schreier--Witt extensions of a reduced Witt vector of Schmid, Kanesaka--Sekiguchi and Thomas for finite residue fields \cite{Sch37,KS79,Th}. Since $\overline{U}_n\to\mathbb{P}^1_t$ and the class $[t]$ are defined over $\mathbb{F}_p$, and lower breaks do not change under the constant field extension $\mathbb{F}_p((1/t))\subset k((1/t))$, this finite-residue-field case applies directly (see also \cite[Thm.~2.3]{EK25} for arbitrary perfect residue fields, \cite[Thm.~1]{Ga} for the top break of cyclic covers of curves over a perfect field, and \cite{Bry83})
(if the coordinates $a_i$ of a reduced vector that are not regular at $\infty$ have pole orders $m_i$, then $u_j=\max\{p^{\,j-1-i}m_i:i<j,\ a_i\text{ not regular}\}$), the upper breaks are $u_j=p^{j-1}$. Then \eqref{eq:herbrand} gives $l_1=1$ and $l_{j+1}=l_j+p^j(p^j-p^{j-1})=l_j+(p-1)p^{2j-1}$, which is \eqref{eq:ln}; the closed form and the recursion are elementary.
(b) $\overline{U}_m\to\overline{U}_{m-1}$ is a $\mathbb{Z}/p$-cover, \'etale over $U_{m-1}$ (as $U_m\to\mathbb{A}^1$ is \'etale), totally ramified at $\infty$ with break $l_m(p)$; apply Lemma~\ref{lem:ASlayer}(c).
(c) Put $M_m:=l_m(p)-p(2g(\overline{U}_{m-1})-1)$. Then $M_1=1+p$. By (b), $p(2g(\overline{U}_m)-1)=p^2(2g(\overline{U}_{m-1})-1)-p^2+p(p-1)(l_m+1)+p$, and $p^2(2g(\overline{U}_{m-1})-1)=p(l_m-M_m)$; together these give $p(2g(\overline{U}_m)-1)=p^2l_m-pM_m$, i.e.\ $M_{m+1}=l_{m+1}-p^2l_m+pM_m=pM_m+1-p$ by (a). By induction $M_m=p^m+1$.

label: def:lambda
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:lambda}
Let $G$ be a finite group. For a smooth projective curve $C$ over $k$ with a faithful $G$-action and a $G$-fixed $k$-point $\infty$, let $\lambda(C,\infty)$ be the smallest element prime to $p$ of the Weierstrass semigroup $H(\infty)$ (the set of pole orders at $\infty$ of functions regular on $C\smallsetminus\{\infty\}$), and let $\lambda_k(G)$ be the minimum of $\lambda(C,\infty)$ over all such pairs ($\lambda_k(G)=\infty$ if none exists).

label: thm:B
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:B}
Let $n\ge1$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item The top layer $\overline{U}_n\to\overline{U}_{n-1}$ has an Artin--Schreier generator $y\in\mathcal O(U_n)$ with $y^p-y=c\in\mathcal O(U_{n-1})$ and $v_\infty(c)=-l_n$ on $\overline{U}_{n-1}$; then $v_\infty(y)=-l_n$ on $\overline{U}_n$.
\item $\lambda(\overline{U}_n,\infty)\le l_n(p)$.
\item $D(U_n)$ contains an integer prime to $p$ and $\le l_n(p)$; hence
\[
d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le l_n(p).
\]
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) For $n=1$ take $y=y_0$, $c=t$. Let $n\ge2$. By the definition of $U_n$, $U_n\subset U_{n-1}\times\mathbb{A}^1$ is the curve $y_{n-1}^p-y_{n-1}=c_0$, where $c_0\in k[y_0,\dots,y_{n-2}]\subseteq\mathcal O(U_{n-1})$ is minus the part of $(\wp y)_{n-1}$ not involving $y_{n-1}$; so $y_{n-1}$ is an Artin--Schreier generator of $k(\overline{U}_n)/k(\overline{U}_{n-1})$, regular on $U_n$. Every Artin--Schreier generator $c'\in\mathcal O(U_{n-1})$ of this layer has $v_\infty(c')<0$: otherwise $c'$ is regular on the projective curve $\overline{U}_{n-1}$, hence constant, and the layer would split. We modify $c_0$ by elements $\wp(b)$, $b\in\mathcal O(U_{n-1})$, until its pole order is prime to $p$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:ASlayer}(b) the final pole order is then $l_n$. Suppose the current generator $c'$ has pole order $pa$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:ASlayer}(b), $l_n<pa$. It suffices to know that $a\in H(\infty)$ on $\overline{U}_{n-1}$: then there is $b\in\mathcal O(U_{n-1})$ with $v_\infty(b)=-a$, which after scaling by a constant ($k$ is algebraically closed) has $b^p$ with the same leading term as $c'$ with respect to a fixed uniformiser, and $c'-\wp(b)$ has smaller pole order. Since the pole orders strictly decrease, the process stops, and $y:=y_{n-1}-\sum b$ is the required generator; $v_\infty(y)=-l_n$ because $v_\infty(c)=-pl_n$ on $\overline{U}_n$.

It remains to see $a\in H(\infty)$. For $n=2$, $\overline{U}_1=\mathbb{P}^1_{y_0}$ and $H(\infty)=\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$. For $n\ge3$, Lemma~\ref{lem:lnformula}(c), which rests on \cite{Sch37,EK25}, gives $pa>l_n=p(2g(\overline{U}_{n-1})-1)+p^n+1$, so $a\ge2g(\overline{U}_{n-1})$, and every integer $\ge2g(\overline{U}_{n-1})$ lies in $H(\infty)$ by Riemann--Roch.

For $n=2$ the reduction is not even needed: from the ghost component $w_1(x)=x_0^p+px_1$ one gets $(\wp y)_1=y_1^p-y_1+Q(y_0)$ with
\[
Q(y_0)=\tfrac1p\bigl(y_0^{p^2}-y_0^p-(y_0^p-y_0)^p\bigr)=y_0^{p^2-p+1}+(\text{terms of lower degree}),
\]
since the term $\binom p{p-1}y_0^{p(p-1)}(-y_0)$ of $(y_0^p-y_0)^p$ contributes $+y_0^{p^2-p+1}$ to $Q$, the term $y_0^{p^2}$ cancels, and the remaining terms have degree $(p-1)i+p<p^2-p+1$ ($0\le i\le p-2$). As $v_\infty(y_0)=-1$ on $\overline{U}_1=\mathbb{P}^1_{y_0}$, the generator $c_0=-Q(y_0)$ already has pole order $p^2-p+1$, prime to $p$; so $y_1$ is a regular reduced generator and $l_2(p)=p^2-p+1$, independently of \cite{Th}. At $(p,n)=(2,3)$ a single reduction step, with $b=y_0^2y_1$, gives the reduced generator $y_2+y_0^2y_1$ of pole order $11$ (Appendix~\ref{app:genus}); so $l_3(2)=11$, again independently of \cite{Th}.

(b) By (a), $y$ is regular on $U_n$ with pole order $l_n$, prime to $p$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:ASlayer}(b)).

(c) $X:={}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!\overline{U}_n$ is a smooth projective geometrically integral $K$-curve with the $K$-point $\infty'$ (the twist of $\infty$), and its free locus is $X\smallsetminus\{\infty'\}$, as $\overline{U}_n^{\mathrm{free}}=U_n$. Riemann--Roch dimensions $\ell(d\infty')$ are invariant under the base change to $L$, where $(X,\infty')$ becomes $(\overline{U}_n,\infty)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:twistL}, Fact~\ref{fact:pic}(b)); so by (a) there is $f\in K(X)$ with pole divisor exactly $l_n\infty'$. For $c\in K$ the divisor $\operatorname{div}(f-c)+l_n\infty'$ is effective, $K$-rational, of degree $l_n$, and supported on the free locus. The degrees of its closed points, counted with multiplicity, sum to $l_n$, which is prime to $p$; so one of them has degree $e$ prime to $p$, $e\le l_n$, and it is free. Hence $e\in D(U_n)$, and Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:freepoint}] gives $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes F')\le1$ for its residue field $F'$, of degree $e$; so $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le e$.

label: thm:lambda
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{thm:lambda}
Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$ with a faithful action of $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ fixing a point $\infty$. If $f\in k(C)$ is regular on $C\smallsetminus\{\infty\}$ and $p\nmid v_\infty(f)$, then
\[
-v_\infty(f)\ \ge\ l(C,\infty)\ \ge\ l_n(p).
\]
Consequently $\lambda(C,\infty)\ge l_n(p)$ for every such pair, $\lambda(\overline{U}_n,\infty)=l_n(p)$, and
\[
\lambda_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^n)=l_n(p)=1+(p-1)\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}p^{2j-1}.
\]
head: environment
name: curves with a fixed point

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\sigma=g^{p^{n-1}}$; then $C\to C/\langle\sigma\rangle$ is a $\mathbb{Z}/p$-cover totally ramified at $\infty$ with lower break $l(C,\infty)$. We have $\sigma f\ne f$: otherwise $f\in k(C/\langle\sigma\rangle)$ and $v_\infty(f)\in p\mathbb{Z}$, as $\infty$ has ramification index $p$ over its image. Since $\sigma$ preserves $C\smallsetminus\{\infty\}$, the nonzero function $\sigma f-f$ is regular on $C\smallsetminus\{\infty\}$, hence is a constant or has a pole at $\infty$: $v_\infty(\sigma f-f)\le0$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:ASlayer}(a), $v_\infty(\sigma f-f)=v_\infty(f)+l(C,\infty)$. Hence $-v_\infty(f)\ge l(C,\infty)$.

For the second inequality, the completion of $k(C)$ at $\infty$ is a totally ramified cyclic extension of degree $p^n$ of a field $k((x))$, so its upper breaks satisfy $u_{j+1}\ge p\,u_j$ (Schmid \cite{Sch37}; this inequality is the only consequence of the break formula needed here). It follows from the formula $u_{j+1}=\max\{pu_j,m_j\}$ for a reduced Witt vector of the extension (every class in $W_n(k((x)))/\wp$ has a reduced representative, each coordinate being regular or having a pole of order prime to $p$, since the residue field $k$ is perfect; total ramification forces $u_1=m_0\ge1$).
Since $u_1=l_1\ge1$, we get $u_j\ge p^{j-1}$ and $u_{j+1}-u_j\ge(p-1)u_j\ge(p-1)p^{j-1}$, and \eqref{eq:herbrand} gives
\[
l(C,\infty)=u_1+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}p^j(u_{j+1}-u_j)\ \ge\ 1+(p-1)\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}p^{2j-1}=l_n(p),
\]
the last equality being \eqref{eq:ln}. The consequences follow, using Theorem~\ref{thm:B}(b) for $\lambda(\overline{U}_n,\infty)\le l_n(p)$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
(i) The first inequality of Proposition~\ref{thm:lambda} uses none of the ramification formulas; with Theorem~\ref{thm:B}(a) it gives $\lambda(\overline{U}_n,\infty)=l(\overline{U}_n,\infty)$ directly. The second uses only $u_{j+1}\ge p\,u_j$. The closed formula \eqref{eq:ln} enters for the value of $l_n(p)$, for the sharpness (that $\overline{U}_n$ attains the bound) and, for $n\ge3$, for $a\in H(\infty)$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:B}(a); it is proved here directly for $n\le2$ and for $(p,n)=(2,3)$.
(ii) By Proposition~\ref{thm:lambda}, $l_n(p)$ is the smallest $d$ prime to $p$ for which a twisted curve ${}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!C$ with a $G$-fixed point carries a function with pole divisor exactly $d\infty'$, i.e.\ the smallest degree of a pencil $|d\infty'|$ to which the degree-sum argument in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:B}(c) applies. That this is nevertheless the true value of $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})$ is Theorem~\ref{thm:ptp}, which also controls fibres of degree divisible by $p$.
(iii) The naive argument ``$\ell(d\infty')\ge2$ for $d\ge g(\overline{U}_n)+1$, take $d$ prime to $p$'' does not work: the fibres of $f\in\mathcal L(d\infty')$ have degree equal to the actual pole order of $f$, which lies in the Weierstrass semigroup and may be divisible by $p$. At $(2,3)$, $g(\overline{U}_3)=7$ and the semigroup of $\infty$ is $\langle4,6,11\rangle$, whose gaps are $\{1,2,3,5,7,9,13\}$ (Appendix~\ref{app:genus}): every function regular on $U_3$ with pole order $\le10$ has even pole order.

label: thm:qRV
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:qRV}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item Let $(C,\infty)$ be as in Definition~\ref{def:lambda}. For every $G$-torsor $\tau$ over every field $F\supseteq k$ there is a separable extension $F'/F$ with $p\nmid[F':F]\le\lambda(C,\infty)$ and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')\le1$. Hence
\[
d_1^{(p')}(\tau)\le d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le\lambda_k(G)\qquad\text{for every }\tau .
\]
\item For $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$: $\lambda_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^n)=l_n(p)=1+(p-1)\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}p^{2j-1}$, realised by $(\overline{U}_n,\infty)$, and no pair $(C,\infty)$ gives a smaller bound in \textup{(a)} (Proposition~\ref{thm:lambda}). So every $\mathbb{Z}/p^n$-torsor over every $F\supseteq k$ becomes one-dimensional over a separable extension of degree prime to $p$ and at most $l_n(p)$; this bound is $1$ for $n=1$, $p^2-p+1$ for $n=2$, $11$ at $(2,3)$, $43$ at $(2,4)$, and it is attained by $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:ptp}). Together with Proposition~\ref{prop:trunc}, $d_1(\tau)\le p^{n-1}$ for every $\mathbb{Z}/p^n$-torsor $\tau$ (note $p^{n-1}\le l_n(p)$).
\item For an arbitrary finite $G$ with Sylow $p$-subgroup $G_p$: $d_1^{(p')}(\tau)\le[G:G_p]\cdot\lambda_k(G_p)$ for every $G$-torsor $\tau$ over every $F\supseteq k$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: quantitative Reichstein--Vistoli

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) The field $F\supseteq k$ is infinite. Let $X={}^{\tau}\!C$ and $\infty'\in X(F)$ the twist of $\infty$. The non-free locus $N\subset C$ is a finite $G$-stable set (fixed points of the nontrivial elements of a group acting faithfully on a curve), so ${}^{\tau}\!N$ is a finite set of closed points of $X$. The Weierstrass semigroup of $\infty'$ on $X$ equals $H(\infty)$ (Riemann--Roch dimensions are invariant under base change, and $(X,\infty')_{\bar F}\cong(C,\infty)_{\bar F}$), so there is $f\in F(X)$ with pole divisor exactly $\lambda\infty'$, $\lambda=\lambda(C,\infty)$. The fibres $f=c$, $c\in F$, are pairwise disjoint effective $F$-rational divisors of degree $\lambda$ not containing $\infty'$; all but finitely many avoid ${}^{\tau}\!N$. For such a fibre the degrees of its closed points, counted with multiplicity, sum to $\lambda$, which is prime to $p$; so one closed point has degree $e$ prime to $p$, $e\le\lambda$, and lies in the free locus. Its residue field $F'$ is separable over $F$ (its degree is prime to $p$), and Theorem~[A,\,\ref{A-thm:geom}] with $Z=C^{\mathrm{free}}$ gives $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F')\le1$. The chain of inequalities is Proposition~[A,\,\ref{A-prop:vers}].

(b) The equality is Proposition~\ref{thm:lambda}, and the bound for every torsor is (a). Sharpness for $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is Theorem~\ref{thm:ptp}. The last claim is Proposition~\ref{prop:trunc} applied to an arbitrary torsor: $\operatorname{ed}^{[p^{n-1}]}_k(\tau_a)\le\operatorname{trdeg}_kk(a_0)\le1$.

(c) $T/G_p\to\operatorname{Spec} F$ is \'etale of degree $[G:G_p]$, so it has a field factor $F_1$ with $p\nmid[F_1:F]\le[G:G_p]$; over $F_1$ the torsor has a point of $T/G_p$, hence $\tau\otimes F_1\cong\operatorname{Ind}_{G_p}^G\tau_p$ for a $G_p$-torsor $\tau_p$ over $F_1$. By (a) there is $F_2/F_1$ with $p\nmid[F_2:F_1]\le\lambda_k(G_p)$ and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_p\otimes F_2)\le1$, and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau\otimes F_2)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_p\otimes F_2)$ by Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:ind}].

label: rem:qRV
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:qRV}
(i) What is new relative to \cite{RV18} and to Proposition~\ref{prop:tail}(b),(c): the explicit bound, its uniformity in $\tau$, and the identification of the optimal bound obtainable from curves with a fixed point with the ramification invariant $l_n(p)$ (Proposition~\ref{thm:lambda}). The mechanism, a free point on a curve with a fixed point, is that of \cite[Lemma~9.1]{RS22} and of Proposition~\ref{prop:tail}(c); what replaces largeness is Riemann--Roch on the twisted curve.
(ii) A crude bound valid for every $(C,\infty)$ is $\lambda(C,\infty)\le$ the least integer prime to $p$ that is $\ge2g(C)$, since $H(\infty)\supseteq[2g(C),\infty)$; at $(2,3)$ this gives $15$ against $11$.
(iii) By Theorem~\ref{thm:ptp}, $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=l_n(p)$: the bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:qRV}(a) is sharp for $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$, and by Proposition~\ref{thm:lambda} it cannot be improved from any pair $(C,\infty)$.
(iv) The uniform statement is a statement about $\sup_\tau$: by Proposition~[A,\,\ref{A-prop:vers}] it is equivalent to the bound for $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ alone.

label: thm:ptp
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:ptp}
Let $n\ge2$ and let $F'/K$ be a finite extension of degree prime to $p$ with $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes_KF')\le1$. Then
\[
[F':K]\ \ge\ l_n(p)=1+(p-1)\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}p^{2j-1}=\frac{p^{2n-1}+1}{p+1}.
\]
Consequently $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=l_n(p)$, and no smooth projective curve with a faithful $\mathbb{Z}/p^n$-action has a free closed point of degree $d<l_n(p)$, $p\nmid d$, on its twist.
head: environment
name: the first prime-to-$p$ jump degree

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $p\nmid d:=[F':K]$, the extension $F'/K$ is separable and $F'\cap L=K$ (an intermediate field $K_i\subseteq F'$ has degree $p^i\mid d$), so $L\otimes_KF'$ is a field and Setup~\ref{setup:witness} applies. Let $C$, $P$, $\xi$, $e=[\kappa(\xi):K]$, $\Delta=\tfrac de\,\psi(\eta)$ and $D_0$ be as there; by Proposition~\ref{prop:rigid}(b),(c), $D_0$ is an effective divisor of degree $d$ on the faithful $G$-curve $C$, $\Delta\sim D_0\otimes_kL$, $\ell(D_0)\ge2$, and $h^*D_0\sim D_0$ for all $h\in G$.

Step 1: $e\ge2$. If $e=1$ then $\xi$ is a free $K$-point of $X={}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!C$, and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le1$ by Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:freepoint}], contradicting $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ge2$ (Remark~\ref{rem:rigid-d1}).

Motivation for Step 2. Purity of $L$ over $k$ has so far only made the class of $D_0$ constant. Step 2 uses the other half of the hypothesis, that the witness is a single closed point of degree $e\ge2$ over $L$: a fixed point of $|D_0|$ would be an $L$-rational point of $\operatorname{Supp}\Delta$, which is impossible. Base-point-freeness is what lets Step 5 find $f$ with prescribed order at the fixed point $\infty$.

Step 2: $|D_0|$ has no base points. Let $B$ be the fixed part of $|D_0|$, the largest effective divisor with $\mathcal L(D_0-B)=\mathcal L(D_0)$. By Fact~\ref{fact:pic}(b), $\mathcal L(D_0\otimes L)=\mathcal L(D_0)\otimes L$, so the fixed part of $|D_0\otimes L|$ is $B\otimes L$. As $\Delta\in|D_0\otimes L|$ is effective, $\Delta\ge B\otimes L$. If $B\ne0$, the support of $\Delta$ would contain a point of $\operatorname{Supp}(B\otimes L)$, which is $L$-rational. But $\operatorname{Supp}\Delta=\{\psi(\eta)\}$ is a single closed point with residue field $\kappa(\xi)\otimes_KL$, of degree $e\ge2$ over $L$. So $B=0$.

Step 3: a $G$-invariant divisor in the class of $D_0$. Put $\mathcal P=k(C)^\times/k^\times$. The sequence $0\to\mathcal P\to\operatorname{Div}(C)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to0$ is $G$-equivariant. From $0\to k^\times\to k(C)^\times\to\mathcal P\to0$ and $H^1(G,k(C)^\times)=0$ (Hilbert~90, $G$ acting faithfully on $k(C)$) we get an injection $H^1(G,\mathcal P)\hookrightarrow H^2(G,k^\times)=k^\times/(k^\times)^{p^n}=0$ ($G$ is cyclic and $k$ is algebraically closed). Hence $\operatorname{Div}(C)^G\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)^G$ is onto, and since $[D_0]\in\operatorname{Pic}(C)^G$ there is a $G$-invariant divisor $E\sim D_0$. It need not be effective.

Step 4: a fixed point. Write $E=\sum_xn_xx$. The orbits of $G$ have $p$-power size, so $d=\deg E\equiv\sum_{x\ G\text{-fixed}}n_x\pmod p$. As $p\nmid d$ there is a $G$-fixed point $\infty$ with $p\nmid m:=n_\infty$. In particular the faithful action fixes $\infty$, and $\infty$ is totally ramified in $C\to C/G$.

Step 5: the function $f$. By Step~2 and $E\sim D_0$, $\infty$ is not a base point of $|E|$, so there is $f\in\mathcal L(E)=\{f:\operatorname{div} f+E\ge0\}$ whose divisor $\operatorname{div} f+E$ has coefficient $0$ at $\infty$, i.e.\ $v_\infty(f)=-m$ with $p\nmid m$.

Step 6: the bound. Let $\sigma=g^{p^{n-1}}$ generate the last non-trivial ramification group at $\infty$ and let $l=l(C,\infty)$ be the last lower break, so that $C\to C/\langle\sigma\rangle$ satisfies the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:ASlayer} with lower break $l$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:ASlayer}(a), applied to $f$ (valid for either sign of $v_\infty(f)$ as $p\nmid v_\infty(f)$), $h:=\sigma f-f\ne0$ and $v_\infty(h)=-m+l$. Since $E$ is $\sigma$-invariant, $h\in\mathcal L(E)$. So $\operatorname{div} h+E\ge0$ is an effective divisor of degree $d$ with coefficient $v_\infty(h)+m=l$ at $\infty$, whence $d\ge l(C,\infty)\ge l_n(p)$ by Proposition~\ref{thm:lambda}.

The consequence $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=l_n(p)$ follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:qRV}(b). A free closed point $\xi$ of degree $d$ on the twist of a faithful curve has residue field $F'$ with $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes F')\le1$ (Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:freepoint}]) and $[F':K]=d$, so $d\ge l_n(p)$ if $p\nmid d$.

label: cor:ptpvalues
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:ptpvalues}
$d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=p^2-p+1$ for $n=2$ and every $p$ \textup{(}$=3$ for $p=2$, $7$ for $p=3$, $21$ for $p=5$\textup{)}; $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=11$ at $(2,3)$ and $61$ at $(3,3)$; $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=43$ at $(2,4)$. Thus the bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:qRV} is sharp for $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ in every case.

label: rem:ptpmech
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:ptpmech}
The mechanism is different from the pencil argument of Section~\ref{ss:rigid}: for a degree $d$ prime to $p$ the base-point-freeness of the witness system and the invariance of its class (a purely cohomological fact for cyclic $G$ over an algebraically closed field) force a fixed point of the invariant divisor, where the last Artin--Schreier layer $\sigma$ produces a function in $\mathcal L(E)$ with a controlled pole. This is also why the argument needs $p\nmid d$: for $p\mid d$ the divisor $E$ need not have a $G$-fixed point of multiplicity prime to $p$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:N1} (the PGL$_\ell$ argument) takes over.

label: cor:large
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:large}
Let $(C,\infty)$ be as in Definition~\ref{def:lambda} (e.g.\ $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ and $(C,\infty)=(\overline{U}_n,\infty)$), let $F\supseteq k$ be a large field (Fact~[A,\,\ref{A-fact:rs}]; e.g.\ $F_0((t))$, a henselian nontrivially valued field, a $p$-closed field), $\tau$ a $G$-torsor over $F$, $X={}^{\tau}\!C$, $\infty'\in X(F)$ the twist of $\infty$, and $f\in F(X)$ with pole divisor $\lambda\infty'$, $\lambda=\lambda(C,\infty)$, as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:qRV}(a).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $X(F)$ is dense in $X$. All but finitely many fibres $f=c$, $c\in F$, are free $F$-rational divisors of degree $\lambda$ of the pencil $|\lambda\infty'|$, and the fibres through the (infinitely many) free $F$-points of $X$ contain an $F$-point.
\item $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)\le1$, i.e.\ $d_1(\tau)=1$: the profile of every $G$-torsor over a large field is $(\le1,\dots,\le1,0)$, with the terminal $0$ at $d_0(\tau)=|\operatorname{im}\varphi_\tau|$.
\item For $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$: $\tau\cong\tau_{[t]}$ for some $t\in F$, i.e.\ every class in $W_n(F)/\wp$ is Teichm\"uller, with no finite extension of $F$ needed.
\end{enumerate}
Part \textup{(b)} is \cite[Lemma~9.1]{RS22} (Fact~\ref{fact:rsd}) for the groups admitting a pair $(C,\infty)$; its proof below is theirs, specialised to the curve $C$, and uses only the density of $X(F)$, not the pencil.
head: environment
name: large fields

title: Proof
body_md: (a) $X$ is a smooth projective geometrically integral $F$-curve with the smooth $F$-point $\infty'$, so $X(F)$ is dense in $X$ by the definition of a large field. The non-free locus ${}^{\tau}\!N$ is a finite set of closed points, so only finitely many fibres of $f$ meet it; every other fibre $f=c$ is an effective $F$-rational divisor of degree $\lambda$ supported in the free locus. A free $F$-point $P$ of $X$ (there are infinitely many, by density and finiteness of ${}^{\tau}\!N\cup\{\infty'\}$) has $f(P)=c\in F$ since $P\ne\infty'$, and lies on the fibre $f=c$. (b) A free $F$-point is a $G$-equivariant morphism $T\to C^{\mathrm{free}}$ (Fact~[A,\,\ref{A-fact:rs}](a)), and Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:freepoint}] with $Z=C^{\mathrm{free}}$ gives $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau)\le1$; hence $d_1(\tau)=1$. The terminal value and its position are Proposition~[A,\,\ref{A-prop:shape}](a),(e) and Proposition~[A,\,\ref{A-prop:d0}](a) ($k$ is algebraically closed). (c) As in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:tail}(c): a free $F$-point of ${}^{\tau}\!\overline{U}_n$ lies in ${}^{\tau}\!U_n$ and is $y=x+h$ with $\wp(x)=a$ the class of $\tau$, $h\inW_n(F)$ and $\wp(y)=[t]$, $t\in F$; so $a\equiv[t]$.

label: rem:large
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:large}
(i) The proof of \cite[Lemma~9.1]{RS22} is the same mechanism: over a large field, weak versality (the fixed point $\infty$, i.e.\ the $F$-point $\infty'$) upgrades to versality (Fact~[A,\,\ref{A-fact:rs}](b)), which is the density statement in (a). Theorem~\ref{thm:qRV} is what survives over a non-large field: the pencil $|\lambda\infty'|$ still consists of free $F$-rational divisors, but they need not contain $F$-points, and the profile records how they split, into closed points of degree $\le\lambda$ prime to $p$ at worst.
(ii) The instance $(p,n)=(2,2)$: over $K_2=k(s_0,s_1)$ the twisted curve $E'\colon w^2+w=u(u+1)(u+s_0)+s_1$ has $E'(K_2)=\{\infty'\}$, and the pencil $|3\infty'|=\langle1,u,w\rangle$ ($\lambda=l_2(2)=3$) has as free members the line sections, each a single cubic point; so $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_2)=3=l_2(2)$ and $d_1(\tau_2)=2$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:n2}). Over the large field $F=K_2((t))$ the same curve acquires the points near $\infty'$: with the local parameter $u/w$ at $\infty'$ put $u/w=t$, i.e.\ $w=u/t$, and $u=t^{-2}v$; the equation becomes
\[
v^3+v^2+(1+s_0)t^2v^2+t^3v+s_0t^4v+s_1t^6=0,
\]
which has the simple root $v\equiv1\bmod t$ (the derivative is $v^2+t^3+s_0t^4\equiv1$), so Hensel's lemma gives a unique $v\in K_2[[t]]$ with $v(0)=1$, in fact $v\in\mathbb{F}_2[s_0,s_1][[t]]$:
\begin{align*}
u&=t^{-2}+(1+s_0)+t+s_0t^2+(1+s_0)t^3+(1+s_0+s_0^2+s_1)t^4+(1+s_0^2)t^5+O(t^6),\\
w&=u/t=t^{-3}+(1+s_0)t^{-1}+1+s_0t+(1+s_0)t^2+O(t^3)
\end{align*}
(the coefficients are obtained by the Hensel recursion, and one checks directly that substituting $v=t^2u$ into the cubic gives $0$ modulo $t^8$; the identities hold in $\mathbb{F}_2[s_0,s_1]$); note that $u$ has no $t^{-1}$ term ($v\equiv1\bmod t^2$). This is a free $F$-point of $E'^\circ={}^{\tau_2}\!U_2$, and as in Theorem~\ref{thm:n2}(b) (the identity $s+\wp h=[(s+\wp h)_0]$ for $h=(u,w)$ with $(s+\wp h)_1=0$ holds over every extension of $K_2$) the generic $\mathbb{Z}/4$-torsor is Teichm\"uller over $K_2((t))$:
\[
(s_0,s_1)\equiv[x],\qquad x=s_0+u^2+u=t^{-4}+t^{-2}+s_0^2+t+(1+s_0)t^2+(1+s_0)t^3+O(t^4).
\]
So $d_1(\tau_2\otimes K_2((t)))=1$, against $d_1(\tau_2)=2$ and $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_2)=3$ over $K_2$; and $d_0(\tau_2\otimes K_2((t)))=4$ still, by Proposition~[A,\,\ref{A-prop:d0}](b), since $K_2$ is algebraically closed in $K_2((t))$.
(iii) In general, over a large field every class is Teichm\"uller (part (c)), which is the ``local form'' of Proposition~\ref{prop:tail}(c) without the finite prime-to-$p$ extension; in profile language, $d_1=1$. The profile is the invariant of what happens before the field is large.

label: lem:hilbertfree
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:hilbertfree}
Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$ with a faithful action of $G=\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ and a $G$-fixed point $\infty$, and let $d\ge1$. Suppose some $f_0\in\mathcal L(d\infty)$ has pole order exactly $d$ and $df_0\ne0$. Then ${}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!C$ has a free closed point of degree $d$; that is, $d\in D(C)$.
head: environment
name: Hilbert irreducibility on a twisted curve

title: Proof
body_md: Let $X={}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!C$ and $\infty'\in X(K)$ the twist of $\infty$. Let $V=\mathcal L_X(d\infty')$, $V_1=\mathcal L_X((d-1)\infty')$ and $V_2=\{f\in V:df=0\}$, the kernel of the $K$-linear map $d\colon V\to\Omega_{K(X)/K}$. Under the base change to $L$ and the isomorphism $\psi$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:twistL}, these become $\mathcal L(d\infty)\otimes_kL$, $\mathcal L((d-1)\infty)\otimes_kL$ and the kernel of $d$ on $\mathcal L(d\infty)\otimes_kL$ (Fact~\ref{fact:pic}(b); kernels commute with flat base change). As $f_0\otimes1$ lies in neither of the last two, $V_1$ and $V_2$ are proper subspaces of $V$, and since $K$ is infinite there is $f\in V\smallsetminus(V_1\cup V_2)$. Then $f$ has pole divisor exactly $d\infty'$, so $[K(X):K(f)]=d$ \cite[Thm.~1.4.11]{St}. As $X$ is geometrically integral, $K(X)/K$ is separably generated and $\Omega_{K(X)/K}$ is one-dimensional, spanned by $df\ne0$; hence $\Omega_{K(X)/K(f)}=0$ and $K(X)/K(f)$ is separable \cite[II.8.6A]{Hart77}. Choose $\theta\in K(X)$ integral over $K[f]$ with $K(X)=K(f)(\theta)$, with minimal polynomial $P(f,Y)\in K[f][Y]$. For all $c\in K$ outside a finite set, the fibre of $f\colon X\to\mathbb{P}^1_K$ over $c$ is $\operatorname{Spec} K[Y]/(P(c,Y))$ (the order $K[f][\theta]$ agrees with the integral closure of $K[f]$ in $K(X)$ away from finitely many points) and avoids the finite non-free locus of $X$ (the fibres are pairwise disjoint). The field $K=k(s_0,\dots,s_{n-1})$ is Hilbertian \cite[Thm.~13.4.2]{FJ}, so $P(c,Y)$ is irreducible over $K$ for all $c$ in a separable Hilbert subset of $K$, which is nonempty and remains so after removing finitely many elements \cite[\S12.1]{FJ}. For such $c$ the fibre is a single free closed point of degree $d$.

label: prop:G1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:G1}
Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve with faithful $G_2$-action. Then ${}^{\tau_2}\!C$ has no free $K_2$-point; in fact ${}^{\tau_2}\!C(K_2)$ is in bijection with $C^{G_2}(k)$. Consequently $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^2)=2$ and $d_1(\tau_2)\ge2$.
head: environment
name: rational points of twisted $\Z/p^2$-curves

title: Proof
body_md: A $K_2$-point is an equivariant $f\colon\operatorname{Spec} L_2\to C$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:imageB} the closure $Y$ of its image is a $G_2$-stable point (then a fixed $k$-point, and $f$ is constant) or all of $C$. In the latter case $k(C)\subseteq L_2=k(z_0,z_1)$, so $C\cong\mathbb{P}^1$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:curvesB}(iii) and $G_2\hookrightarrow\operatorname{PGL}_2(k)$, contradicting Lemma~\ref{lem:curvesB}(i). So all $K_2$-points are the constant maps to fixed points, none free. Then $d_1(\tau_2)\ge2$ by Corollary~\ref{cor:jumpsB} (for $d=1$, $L_2\otimes K_2=L_2$ is a field), and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^2)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_2)\ge2$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:versal}; $\le2$ is Proposition~\ref{prop:trunc} with $j=0$.

label: thm:n2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:n2}
Let $p=2$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item The curve $\overline{U}_2$ is the supersingular elliptic curve $E_0\colon y_1^2+y_1=y_0^3+y_0^2$ with $G_2$ acting by $(y_0,y_1)\mapsto(y_0+1,y_1+y_0)$, fixing only $\infty$. Its twist is the elliptic curve
\[
E':={}^{\tau_2}\!E_0\colon\quad w^2+w=u(u+1)(u+s_0)+s_1\qquad\text{over }K_2=k(s_0,s_1),
\]
whose origin is the point $\infty'$ (the twist of $\infty$; we write $\infty'_2$ when the curve ${}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!\overline{U}_3$ is also present). Moreover $E'(K_2)=\{\infty'\}$: the Mordell--Weil group of the quartic twist of $E_0$ by the generic $\mathbb{Z}/4$-torsor over $k(s_0,s_1)$ is trivial.
\item Every fibre of $u\colon E'\to\mathbb{P}^1_{K_2}$ over a point $c\in K_2$ is a free closed point of degree $2$, with residue field $K_2(w)$, $w^2+w=c(c+1)(c+s_0)+s_1$, and over it $(s_0,s_1)\equiv[s_0+c^2+c]$.
\item Let $u$ be a root of $P(u):=u^3+(1+s_0)u^2+s_0u+s_1=u(u+1)(u+s_0)+s_1$. Then $F'=K_2(u)$ is a separable cubic extension of $K_2$ and $(s_0,s_1)\equiv[s_0+u^2+u]\bmod\wpW_2(F')$, so $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_2\otimes F')=1$. More precisely, the cubic closed points of $E'$ are exactly the sections by the lines $w=\alpha u+\beta$, $\alpha,\beta\in K_2$; each is a single free point of degree $3$, and over its residue field $(s_0,s_1)$ is Teichm\"uller.
\item $D(U_2)=\mathbb{Z}_{\ge2}$, and the profile of $\tau_2$ is
\[
\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}=2,\quad\operatorname{ed}^{[2]}=\operatorname{ed}^{[3]}=1,\quad\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}=0\ (d\ge4);\qquad d_2=1,\ d_1=2,\ d_1^{(p')}=3,\ d_0=4 .
\]
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: $n=2$, $p=2$: the complete profile

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) $U_2=\{y_0^2+y_0=t,\ y_1^2+y_1+y_0^3+y_0^2=0\}$ by \eqref{eq:wp2} (the $W_2$ part), and $t$ is a function of $y_0$, so $U_2\cong E_0^\circ:=\{y_1^2+y_1=y_0^3+y_0^2\}\subset\mathbb{A}^2$, a smooth affine curve whose projective closure $E_0$ is an elliptic curve with one point $\infty$ at infinity ($a_1=0$, $a_3=1$, $\Delta=1$; supersingular since $a_1=0$ in characteristic $2$, $j=a_1^{12}/\Delta=0$). By \eqref{eq:add2}, $y+1=(y_0+1,y_1+y_0)$, an automorphism of $E_0$ without fixed points on $E_0^\circ$, so $\infty$ is the unique fixed point and $E_0^{\mathrm{free}}=E_0^\circ=U_2$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:S0}(a) (with $n=2$), ${}^{\tau_2}\!U_2=\{h=(u,w)\in\mathbb{A}^2_{K_2}:(s+\wp h)_1=0\}$, and by \eqref{eq:add2}--\eqref{eq:wp2}, $(s+\wp h)_1=s_1+w^2+w+u^3+u^2+s_0(u^2+u)$; so ${}^{\tau_2}\!U_2=E'^\circ:=\{w^2+w=u(u+1)(u+s_0)+s_1\}$, and ${}^{\tau_2}\!E_0$ is its smooth projective closure $E'$, with the single point $\infty'$ at infinity. By Proposition~\ref{prop:G1}, $E'(K_2)={}^{\tau_2}\!E_0(K_2)$ is in bijection with $E_0^{G_2}(k)=\{\infty\}$.

(b) The fibre of $u$ over $c\in K_2$ is $\operatorname{Spec} K_2[w]/(w^2+w-c(c+1)(c+s_0)-s_1)$; it has no $K_2$-point, so it is a field of degree $2$, and its point is free (it lies in $E'^\circ$). Over $K'=K_2(w)$ the vector $h=(c,w)$ satisfies $(s+\wp h)_1=0$, so $s+\wp h=[(s+\wp h)_0]=[s_0+c^2+c]$.

(c) $P\in k(s_0)[u][s_1]$ has degree $1$ in $s_1$ with coprime coefficients $1$ and $u(u+1)(u+s_0)$, hence is irreducible in $k(s_0)[u,s_1]$, hence (Gauss, $P$ monic in $u$) irreducible in $K_2[u]$; an irreducible cubic in characteristic $2$ is separable. By \eqref{eq:add2}--\eqref{eq:wp2}, for $h=(u,0)\inW_2(F')$: $(s+\wp h)_0=s_0+u^2+u$ and $(s+\wp h)_1=s_1+u^3+u^2+s_0u^2+s_0u=P(u)=0$, so $s+\wp h=[s_0+u^2+u]$; equivalently $(u,0)$ is a free $F'$-point of $E'^\circ={}^{\tau_2}\!U_2$, and Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:freepoint}] gives $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_2\otimes F')\le1$; $\ge1$ since $3<4=d_0$ (Proposition~[A,\,\ref{A-prop:d0}]). Cubic points: $E'(K_2)=\{\infty'\}$, so $\operatorname{Pic}^0(E')(K_2)=0$ and every effective $K_2$-divisor of degree $3$ is linearly equivalent to $3\infty'$, i.e.\ is the divisor of zeros of an element of $\mathcal L(3\infty')=\langle1,u,w\rangle$; the divisor of zeros of $a+bu+cw$ contains $\infty'$ iff $c=0$, and then it is $\infty'$ plus a fibre of $u$ (of degree $2$, by (b)); a closed point of degree $3$ is a divisor not containing $\infty'$, so $c\ne0$ and it is a section by a line $w=\alpha u+\beta$ with $\alpha,\beta\in K_2$. Such a section is a single closed point of degree $3$ because a $K_2$-rational component would be a $K_2$-point of $E'^\circ$. It lies in $E'^\circ$, hence is free.

(d) Profile: $\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}=\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/4)=2$; $\operatorname{ed}^{[2]}\le1$ by the degree-$2$ free points of (b) (Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:freepoint}]), equivalently by Remark~\ref{rem:towerp2}; $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}\ge1$ for $d<4$ and $\operatorname{ed}^{[4]}=0$ by Proposition~[A,\,\ref{A-prop:d0}](c). As $d_1^{(p')}$ is odd and $\ge d_1(\tau_2)=2$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:G1}), (c) gives $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_2)=3$. label: thm:23main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:23main}
Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $2$ and $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$ the generic $\mathbb{Z}/8$-torsor over $K=k(s_0,s_1,s_2)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes_KF')\ge2$ for every field extension $F'/K$ of degree $\le3$.
\item $\operatorname{ed}^{[2]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=\operatorname{ed}^{[3]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=2$, hence $d_1(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=4$; the profile is
\[
\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}\in\{2,3\},\qquad\operatorname{ed}^{[2]}=\operatorname{ed}^{[3]}=2,\qquad\operatorname{ed}^{[4]}=\dots=\operatorname{ed}^{[7]}=1,\qquad\operatorname{ed}^{[8]}=0 .
\]
\item For every smooth projective curve $C$ with a faithful $\mathbb{Z}/8$-action, $D(C)\cap\{1,2,3\}=\emptyset$. In particular $D(U_3)\cap\{1,2,3\}=\emptyset$, $4,6\in D(U_3)$, and $\delta_\mathrm{free}(U_3)=4$.
\item No extension of degree $\le3$ realises the first drop of the prime-to-$2$ profile: $\operatorname{ed}^{[3]}_k{}'(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=2$ and $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ge5$. The value $2$ is attained by the cubic extension $K(u)$, $u^3+(1+s_0)u^2+s_0u+s_1=0$; hence $d_2^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\in\{1,3\}$, with $d_2^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=1$ iff $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/8)=2$.
\end{enumerate}
