name: the profile at $(2,3)$ away from the Ledet slot

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) is Theorem~\ref{thm:N1} with $p^{n-1}=4$.
(b) $\operatorname{ed}^{[2]},\operatorname{ed}^{[3]}\ge2$ by (a), and $\le2$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:known23}; $\operatorname{ed}^{[4]}=1$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:known23}, so $d_1=4$.
(c) The first statement is Corollary~\ref{cor:curvepts}. Let $X={}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!\overline{U}_3$ and $d\in\{4,6\}$. Since $d$ lies in the Weierstrass semigroup $\langle4,6,11\rangle$ of $\infty$ on $\overline{U}_3$ (Appendix~\ref{app:genus}) and $\ell(d\infty')-\ell((d-1)\infty')$ is invariant under base change, there is $f\in K(X)$ with pole divisor exactly $d\infty'$. Every fibre $f=c$, $c\in K$, is an effective $K$-rational divisor of degree $d$ in the free locus $X\smallsetminus\{\infty'\}$. Every free closed point has degree $\ge4$ by the first statement, so such a fibre is a single free point of degree $d$ (a point of degree $\ge4$ of multiplicity $\ge2$ would contribute $\ge8$). Hence $4,6\in D(U_3)$ and $\delta_\mathrm{free}(U_3)=4$. No Hilbert irreducibility is needed here.

(d) Lower bounds. By Definition~[A,\,\ref{A-def:profile}], $\operatorname{ed}^{[3]}{}'$ minimises over extensions of degree $1$ or $3$, and $\operatorname{ed}^{[4]}{}'=\operatorname{ed}^{[3]}{}'$; so $\operatorname{ed}^{[3]}{}'(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ge2$ and $d_1^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ge5$ by (a).

Upper bound. Let $u$ be a root of $P(u)=u^3+(1+s_0)u^2+s_0u+s_1=u(u+1)(u+s_0)+s_1$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:n2}(c), $P$ is irreducible and separable over $K_2$. Since $K=K_2(s_2)$ is purely transcendental over $K_2$, $K_2$ is algebraically closed in $K$ and $P$ stays irreducible over $K$ (Gauss's lemma in $K_2[s_2][u]$). So $F':=K(u)=k(s_0,u,s_2)$ is a separable cubic extension of $K$. Put $h=(u,0,0)\inW_3(F')$. By the general translate of Appendix~\ref{app:witt},
\[
s+\wp h=\bigl(s_0+u^2+u,\ P(u),\ s_2+\Phi_2(s_0,s_1,u,0)\bigr)=\bigl(s_0+u^2+u,\ 0,\ s_2+\varphi\bigr),
\]
\[
\varphi=u^7+u^6+s_0(u^6+u^4)+s_0^2(u^4+u^2)+s_0^3(u^2+u)\in k(s_0,u),
\]
where $s_1=u(u+1)(u+s_0)$ has been substituted in $\Phi_2(s_0,s_1,u,0)$. The class $s+\wp h$ lies in $W_3(F_0)$ with $F_0=k(s_0+u^2+u,\ s_2+\varphi)$, $\operatorname{trdeg}_kF_0=2$, so $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes F')\le2$. This is Lemma~\ref{lem:lift} applied to the cubic point of Theorem~\ref{thm:n2}(c), made explicit. Hence $\operatorname{ed}^{[3]}{}'(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=2$.

Jump degree. $\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}{}'=\operatorname{ed}^{[2]}{}'=\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}=\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/8)$ and $\operatorname{ed}^{[3]}{}'=2$, so $d_2^{(p')}(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=1$ if $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/8)=2$ and $=3$ otherwise.

label: lem:fibration
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: curves dominated by a fibration

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider $\phi_\eta\colon V_\eta\dashrightarrow C_{k(B)}$ over $k(B)$. Suppose first that $\phi_\eta$ is dominant. Since $V_\eta$ is geometrically integral, the fibres $V_b$ are integral for $b$ in a dense open subset of $B$ \cite[IV$_3$, \S9.7]{EGA};
and the domain of definition $U$ of $\phi$, a dense open subset of $V$, meets $V_b$ in a dense open subset for $b$ in a dense open subset of $B$. The map $\Phi=(\pi,\phi)\colon U\to B\times C$ is dominant (its generic fibre over $B$ is $\phi_\eta$), so by Chevalley's theorem $\Phi(U)$ contains a dense open $W\subseteq B\times C$; for $b$ in the dense open image of $W$ in $B$, $\phi(U\cap V_b)\supseteq W_b$ is infinite, hence $\phi|_{V_b}$ is dominant. This is (i). Otherwise $\phi_\eta$ has image a closed point $x$ of $C_{k(B)}$, and $k(C)\subseteq\kappa(x)\subseteq k(V_\eta)=k(V)$ with $\kappa(x)$ finite over $k(B)$. As $V_\eta$ is geometrically integral, $k(V)/k(B)$ is a regular extension, so $k(B)$ is algebraically closed in $k(V)$ and $\kappa(x)=k(B)$; hence $k(C)\subseteq k(B)$.

name: explicit extensions with $\ed$ exactly $2$

title: Proof
body_md:
The lower bound is Theorem~\ref{thm:N1} for (a), (b) (degree $\le2$), and for (c) it is proved below.

(a) Write $f=s_2+e+\wp b$, $e\in K_2$, $b\in K$. Over $K'=K(v_f)$, $s_2=\wp(v_f+b)+e$, so $s=(s_0,s_1,e)+\wp V^2(v_f+b)\equiv(s_0,s_1,e)$ by \eqref{eq:Vsplit}; this class is defined over $K_2$, so $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes K')\le2$.

(b) $\operatorname{ed}^{[2]}\le2$ for these fields by Proposition~\ref{prop:known23} (the class over $K(v_1)$ is defined over the transcendence-degree-$2$ field $k(s_0,s_2+s_1^2+s_1v_1)$, and $K(z_0)$ is Proposition~\ref{prop:intermediate}).

(c) The upper bound is [A,\,\S\ref{A-ss:ed},\,(B1)] applied to $K(v_1)\subset K(v_1,v_2)$ and (b). For the lower bound: $L\otimes_KK'$ is a field: $K'/K$ is a $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^2$-extension whose quadratic subfields are $K(v_1)$, $K(v_2)$, $K(v_1+v_2)$, of classes $s_1$, $s_2$, $s_1+s_2$, none $\equiv s_0$ (each has a simple pole at $s_1=\infty$ or $s_2=\infty$, where $s_0$ is regular), so $K'\cap L=K$. Put $y:=v_1+z_1$ and $y':=v_2+z_2$; then $y^2+y=s_1+z_1^2+z_1=z_0^3+z_0^2$ and $y'^2+y'=s_2+z_2^2+z_2=C(z_0,z_1)$ by \eqref{eq:wp2}, so $L(v_1,v_2)=k(z_0,y,z_1,y',z_2)=k(\Sigma\times\mathbb{A}^1_{z_2})$, where
\[
\Sigma:=\{(z_0,y,z_1,y'):\ y^2+y=z_0^3+z_0^2,\ \ y'^2+y'=C(z_0,z_1)\},
\]\[
C(z_0,z_1)=z_1^3+(z_0^3+z_0^2+1)z_1^2+(z_0^3+z_0^2)z_1+z_0^7+z_0^4
\]
($y$ is algebraic over $k(z_0)$, and $[L(v_1):L]=2$ since $z_0^3+z_0^2\notin\wp L$, having odd pole order in $z_0$). $\Sigma$ is an integral surface, fibred over $E_0\colon y^2+y=z_0^3+z_0^2$ via $(z_0,y)$, with generic fibre the affine curve $y'^2+y'=(\text{monic cubic in }z_1)$, which is smooth and geometrically integral of genus $1$ with $j=0$ (Weierstrass form with $a_1=0$, $a_3=1$), hence supersingular. Suppose $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes K')\le1$. By Theorem~[A,\,\ref{A-thm:geom}] and Corollary~\ref{cor:jumpsB} there is a smooth projective curve $C$ with faithful $G$-action and a dominant equivariant rational map $\Sigma\times\mathbb{A}^1\dashrightarrow C$ (the descent field $F_0$ has $\operatorname{trdeg}_kF_0=1$; $\operatorname{trdeg}0$ is impossible as the torsor over $K'$ is a field, hence non-split). Lemma~\ref{lem:fibration} for $\mathrm{pr}_2\colon\Sigma\times\mathbb{A}^1\to\mathbb{A}^1$ gives: $C$ is dominated by $\mathbb{A}^1$ (rational), or by $\Sigma$. In the latter case apply Lemma~\ref{lem:fibration} to $\Sigma\to E_0$: either the general fibre maps dominantly to $C$, or $E_0$ does. (Every closed fibre of $\Sigma\to E_0$ is $y'^2+y'=C(b,z_1)$, a Weierstrass equation with $a_1=0$, $a_3=1$ and monic cubic right-hand side, hence smooth of genus $1$ and supersingular, not only the generic fibre.) Either way $C$ is $\mathbb{P}^1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:curvesB}(iii)) or, by Lemma~\ref{lem:curvesB}(iv), an elliptic curve isogenous to a supersingular one (a nonconstant morphism of elliptic curves is an isogeny up to translation), hence supersingular; neither carries an automorphism of order $8$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:curvesB}(i),(ii)), contradicting faithfulness.

label: rem:23ledet
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:23ledet}
Theorem~\ref{thm:23main} does not decide $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/8)\in\{2,3\}$, and cannot: by monotonicity the slots $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}$ with $d>1$ bound $\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}$ only from below, and $\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}\ge\operatorname{ed}^{[2]}=2$ was known. Both $\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}=2$ and $\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}=3$ are compatible with $d_1=4$. What the theorem does is fix the part of the profile that does not depend on the conjecture. The truncation tower of Proposition~\ref{prop:trunc} is optimal in degree $2$ (the case $j=1$ of Question~\ref{Q4} at this $(p,n)$); no cubic extension beats it; and, unconditionally, no faithful $\mathbb{Z}/8$-curve has a free point of degree $\le3$ on its twist (Theorem~\ref{thm:23main}(c)). So, whatever the value of $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/8)$, faithful curves detect nothing in degrees $\le3$, and the remaining uncertainty sits entirely in dimension $2$: $\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}\le2$ iff some faithful $\mathbb{Z}/8$-surface has a free $K$-point on its twist, and $d_2\in\{1,2\}$ is the same bit (Proposition~\ref{prop:DX}). A proof of the conjecture must therefore be a statement about surfaces at $d=1$: every slot of the profile other than $\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}$ is determined, and none of them carries information about $\operatorname{ed}^{[1]}$.

\label{lem:profileconst}
Let $m\ge1$, $F=k(s_0,\dots,s_{m-1})$, $a\inW_m(F)$ and $t$ transcendental over $F$. Then $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_a\otimes_FF(t))=\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_a)$ for all $d\ge1$.

name: purely transcendental base change of the profile

title: Proof
body_md:
``$\le$'': an extension $F''/F$ of degree $d'\le d$ gives $F''(t)/F(t)$ of degree $d'$, and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_a\otimes F''(t))=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_a\otimes F'')$ by Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:constant}](i).

``$\ge$'': let $F'/F(t)$ have degree $d'\le d$ and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_a\otimes F')\le e$. By Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:pi}] we may assume $F'/F(t)$ separable, so $F'=F(t)(\theta)$ with $\theta$ integral over $F[t]$ and minimal polynomial $P(t,Y)\in F[t][Y]$ monic in $Y$, irreducible in $F[t,Y]$. Put $R=F[t][\theta]\cong F[t][Y]/(P)$, free of rank $d'$ over $F[t]$. By hypothesis $a=b+\wp y$ in $W_m(F')$ with $b\inW_m(F_0)$, $F_0=k(f_1,\dots,f_r)\subseteq F'$, $\operatorname{trdeg}_kF_0=e$, and $y\inW_m(F')$. Let $A\subseteq F_0$ be the $k$-subalgebra generated by the coordinates of $b$; it is a domain of dimension $\le\operatorname{trdeg}_kF_0=e$. Choose $0\ne h\in R$ such that $A\subseteq R[1/h]$ and the coordinates of $y$ lie in $R[1/h]$. The identity $a=b+\wp y$ holds in $W_m(R[1/h])$. For $c\in F$ with $N_{R/F[t]}(h)(c)\ne0$, evaluation $t\mapsto c$ is an $F$-algebra map $\mathrm{ev}_c\colon R[1/h]\to R/(t-c)=F[Y]/(P(c,Y))$. The field $F$ is Hilbertian \cite[Thm.~13.4.2]{FJ}, so $P(c,Y)$ is irreducible for $c$ in a Hilbert subset of $F$, which stays non-empty after removing the finitely many roots of $N_{R/F[t]}(h)$; for such $c$, $F'_c:=R/(t-c)$ is a field of degree $d'$ over $F$. Applying $\mathrm{ev}_c$ gives $a=\mathrm{ev}_c(b)+\wp\,\mathrm{ev}_c(y)$ in $W_m(F'_c)$, because $a$ has coordinates in $F$. The coordinates of $\mathrm{ev}_c(b)$ lie in the image $\mathrm{ev}_c(A)$, a quotient of $A$, so the subfield of $F'_c$ they generate over $k$ has transcendence degree $\le\dim A\le e$. Hence $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_a\otimes F'_c)\le e$ and $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_a)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_a\otimes F(t))$.

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) By Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:pi}] it suffices to consider separable $F'/K$ of degree $\le d$. Truncation is a ring map commuting with $\wp$, so a descent of $\tau_n\otimes F'$ truncates to a descent of $\bar\tau\otimes F'$ of no larger transcendence degree, and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_n\otimes F')\ge\operatorname{ed}_k(\bar\tau\otimes F')\ge\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\bar\tau)=f(n-1,d)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:profileconst}. Conversely $f(n,d)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\bar\tau)+1=f(n-1,d)+1$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:lift} and Lemma~\ref{lem:profileconst}.

(b) By Proposition~[A,\,\ref{A-prop:shape}](b) with $F'=K_1$, $f(n,pd)\le\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_n\otimes K_1)$. By Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:ind}] applied to each extension of $K_1$, $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(\tau_n\otimes K_1)=\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}_k(L/K_1)$, and $L/K_1=\tau_{n-1}\otimes_{F''}F''(z_0)$ with $F''=k(s'_0,\dots,s'_{n-2})$ (proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:intermediate}), whose profile is $f(n-1,d)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:profileconst}.

The last statement: $f(j,p^j)=0$ since $\tau_j$ is split by an extension of degree $p^j$, so $f(n,p^j)=\sum_{m=j+1}^n\delta_m(p^j)\le n-j$, with equality iff all $\delta_m(p^j)=1$.

\label{rem:layersN1}

label: thm:Pn1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Pn1}
Let $n\ge2$, and let $D'(n)$ be the statement: $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_n\otimes_KF')\ge n-1$ for every separable extension $F'/K$ with $2\le[F':K]\le p$ and $L\otimes_KF'$ a field. Then
\[
P(n,1)\iff\mathrm{Led}(n-1)\ \text{and}\ D'(n).
\]
head: environment
name: $P(n,1)$ and Ledet's conjecture

title: Proof
body_md:
Classification. Let $F'/K$ be separable with $[F':K]\le p$. Fix an embedding of $F'$ in an algebraic closure containing $L$. Since $L/K$ is Galois with cyclic group $G$, $L\cap F'=K_i$ for some $0\le i\le n$; $K_i\subseteq F'$ gives $p^i\le[F':K]\le p$. If $i=1$ then $F'=K_1$; if $i=0$ then $L\otimes_KF'$ is a field, since $[LF':F']=[L:L\cap F']$. So $F'=K_1$, or $L\otimes_KF'$ is a field (and $F'=K$ is the case of degree $1$).

The field $K_1$. By Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:ind}] and the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:intermediate}, $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_n\otimes K_1)=\operatorname{ed}_k(L/K_1)$, and $L/K_1=\tau_{n-1}\otimes_{F''}F''(z_0)$ with $z_0$ transcendental over $F''$; so $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_n\otimes K_1)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{n-1})=\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-1})$ by Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:constant}](i) and Lemma~\ref{lem:versal}(c).

($\Rightarrow$) $D'(n)$ holds because $f(n,p)\ge n-1$. Moreover $n-1=f(n,p)\le\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_n\otimes K_1)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-1})\le n-1$, so $\mathrm{Led}(n-1)$.

($\Leftarrow$) Let $F'/K$ have degree $\le p$; by Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:pi}] we may assume it separable. If $F'=K_1$, then $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_n\otimes K_1)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-1})=n-1$ by $\mathrm{Led}(n-1)$. If $F'=K$, then $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_n)\ge\operatorname{ed}_k(\bar\tau)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{n-1})=n-1$ by truncation, Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:constant}](i) and $\mathrm{Led}(n-1)$. In the remaining cases $D'(n)$ applies. Hence $f(n,p)\ge n-1$, and $f(n,p)\le n-1$ is Proposition~\ref{prop:trunc}.

label: cor:Pn1
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: (a) The first claim and $\mathrm{Led}(n-1)$ are Theorem~\ref{thm:Pn1}. For $P(n-1,1)$: $n-1=f(n,p)\le f(n-1,p)+1$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:layers}(a), and $f(n-1,p)\le n-2$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:trunc}. (b) For $n=2$, $L\otimes_KF'$ is a field, so $\tau_2\otimes F'$ is a non-split torsor and $\operatorname{ed}\ge1$. For $n=3$, Theorem~\ref{thm:N1} gives $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_3\otimes F')\ge2$ for every $F'$ of degree $<p^2$; and $\mathrm{Led}(2)$ holds ($\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^2)\le2$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:versal}(c) and $\ge2$ by Remark~\ref{rem:rigid-d1}).

label: rem:Dn
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:Dn}
$D'(n)$ is not known to be easier than $\mathrm{Led}(n-1)$ for $n\ge4$, nor to imply it. Partial and conditional results: if $F'\supseteq K$ is of the form $F_1(w)$, purely transcendental over a finite extension $F_1/F$, with $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{n-1}\otimes_FF_1)=n-1$, then $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_n\otimes F')\ge\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{n-1}\otimes_FF_1(w))=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{n-1}\otimes_FF_1)=n-1$ by truncation and Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:constant}](i); and for $2\le[F':K]<p$, $D'(n)$ would follow from the plateau $f(n-1,p-1)=n-1$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:layers}(a); but that plateau implies $\mathrm{Led}(n-1)$, which is open for $n-1\ge3$, so this is conditional. What is missing is the strictness of the top layer, $\delta_n(p)=1$, for extensions of degree $\le p$ disjoint from $L$.
head: environment

label: prop:Led3lift
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:Led3lift}
Let $n\ge3$, $F=k(s_0,\dots,s_{n-2})$, and let $K_1'=F(z_0)\subset L$ with $z_0^p-z_0=s_0$, so that $K_1=K(z_0)=K_1'(t)$. Then
\[
\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_n\otimes K_1)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-1}),\qquad\operatorname{ed}_k(\bar\tau\otimes K_1)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{n-1}\otimes_FK_1')=\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-2}).
\]
Consequently $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-1})=\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-2})+1$ holds if and only if passing from the truncation $\bar\tau$ to $\tau_n$ over $K_1$ raises the essential dimension by exactly one: $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_n\otimes K_1)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\bar\tau\otimes K_1)+1$. In particular $\mathrm{Led}(3)$, i.e.\ $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/8)=3$, is equivalent to $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_4\otimes K_1)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\bar\tau\otimes K_1)+1$ at $(p,n)=(2,4)$, and, given $\mathrm{Led}(n-2)$, $\mathrm{Led}(n-1)$ is equivalent to the same statement for $n$.
head: environment
name: Ledet's conjecture as a lifting statement

title: Proof
body_md: The first identity is proved in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:Pn1}. For the second, $\bar\tau\otimes_KK_1=(\tau_{n-1}\otimes_FK_1')\otimes_{K_1'}K_1'(t)$, so $\operatorname{ed}_k(\bar\tau\otimes K_1)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{n-1}\otimes_FK_1')$ by Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:constant}](i), and $K_1'$ is the degree-$p$ subfield $F(z_0)$ of the total space of $\tau_{n-1}$, so $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{n-1}\otimes_FK_1')=\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-2})$ by the same argument applied to $\tau_{n-1}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:intermediate} and Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:constant}](i)); this needs $n-1\ge2$.
head: environment

label: rem:N1ledet
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:N1ledet}
(i) By Proposition~\ref{prop:intermediate} and Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:constant}](i), $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes K_1)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{n-1})$ ($K_1$ is purely transcendental over the base field of the generic $\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-1}$-torsor). Hence $\operatorname{ed}^{[p]}_k(\tau_n)=n-1$ would force $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-1})=n-1$: the subgroup formula at $j=1$ for $\mathbb{Z}/p^4$ contains Ledet's conjecture for $\mathbb{Z}/p^3$, and the formula at $j=1$ for all $n$ contains Ledet's conjecture for all $n$ (it gives $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^n)\ge n-1$ only). Theorem~\ref{thm:N1} therefore settles exactly the slots with $n-j\le2$; the slots with $n-j\ge3$ remain open, the first being $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/8)$ at $(2,3)$. (ii) The proof is a statement about curve witnesses, i.e.\ $\operatorname{ed}\le1$. For witnesses of dimension $\ge2$ the first two steps survive in the form of constancy of the class of the point cycle in $\mathrm{CH}_0$, but there is no complete linear system on which $G$ acts, which is what Proposition~\ref{prop:rigidN} uses. In dimension two the class of the zero-cycle $\Delta$ on $X_L$ is still constant in $\mathrm{CH}_0$ (the map $\mathrm{CH}_0(X)\to\mathrm{CH}_0(X_L)$ is surjective for $L/k$ purely transcendental, by homotopy invariance and localisation), hence $G$-invariant. But for $X$ with $A_0(X)=0$, for instance a rational surface, this statement is empty, and for $A_0(X)\ne0$ the class moves in an infinite-dimensional family. We therefore see no analogue of Proposition~\ref{prop:rigidN}, and a lower bound for $\operatorname{ed}^{[d]}$ in the range $\operatorname{ed}\le2$ would need new input.

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) (iii)$\Rightarrow$(ii): let $\phi\colonW_3\dashrightarrow X$ be a $G$-compression and $U\subseteq X$ a dense $G$-stable open subset. The generic point of $W_3$ maps to the generic point of $X$, which lies in $U$; so $\phi$ restricted to the generic point is a $G$-equivariant morphism $\operatorname{Spec} L\to U$, i.e.\ a $K$-point of ${}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!U$ (Fact~[A,\,\ref{A-fact:rs}](a)), and $U$ is $\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}$-weakly versal. (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i): as $G$ acts faithfully on the irreducible $X$, $X^{\mathrm{free}}$ is a dense $G$-stable open subset; its weak versality gives a $K$-point of ${}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!(X^{\mathrm{free}})$, i.e.\ a free $K$-point. (i)$\Rightarrow$(iii): a free $K$-point is a $G$-equivariant $f\colon\operatorname{Spec} L\to X^{\mathrm{free}}$, i.e.\ (as $L=k(W_3)$) a $G$-equivariant rational map $W_3\dashrightarrow X$; the closure $Y$ of its image is irreducible and $G$-stable with faithful $G$-action (Lemma~\ref{lem:imageB}). If $\dim Y\le1$, then ${}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!Y$ has a free $K$-point and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le1$ by Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:freepoint}], contradicting Remark~\ref{rem:rigid-d1}; so $Y=X$ and $f$ is a compression.

For the last statement: if $1\in D(X)$ for some $X$ then $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^3)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\le2$ by Lemma~[A,\,\ref{A-lem:freepoint}] and Lemma~\ref{lem:versal}. Conversely let $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^3)\le2$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:versal} and the identity $\operatorname{ed}_k(Y)=\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_Y)$ of \cite[Section~\ref{A-ss:ed}]{PA} there is a $G$-compression $W_3\dashrightarrow Z$ onto an irreducible generically free $G$-variety of dimension $\le2$, and $\dim Z=2$ since $\operatorname{ed}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})\ge2$. Replace $Z$ by a dense $G$-stable affine open subset, embed it $G$-equivariantly in a finite-dimensional representation (a $G$-stable finite-dimensional subspace of $k[Z]$ generating it) and take the closure in the projective completion: a projective $G$-surface $\bar Z$ birational to $Z$. The resolution of $\bar Z$ obtained by alternately normalising and blowing up the singular locus \cite{Lip78}
terminates in a regular surface by \cite{Lip78}; each step (normalisation, blow-up of the reduced singular locus) is canonical, i.e.\ functorial for isomorphisms of surfaces, so every automorphism of $\bar Z$ lifts to a unique automorphism of the resolution and the resolution carries a $G$-action; it is a smooth projective surface $X$ with faithful $G$-action, $G$-equivariantly birational to $Z$. The compression $W_3\dashrightarrow X$ gives $1\in D(X)$ by (iii)$\Rightarrow$(i).

(b) The fixed point gives the constant map, a $K$-point of ${}^{\tau_{\mathrm{gen}}}\!X$ (Fact~[A,\,\ref{A-fact:rs}](a)).

(c) is Corollary~\ref{cor:jumpsB} and Proposition~\ref{prop:S0}(b) (with $n=3$, $\dim S_0=2$), together with (a) for the value $1$.

label: rem:mirror
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:mirror}
In characteristic $\ne p$ the subgroup formula of \cite[Section~\ref{A-sec:sylow}]{PA} (Florence \cite{Fl08}, Karpenko--Merkurjev) bounds the profile by the minimal faithful representations of subgroups. In characteristic $p$ representations are the wrong envelope: $\operatorname{rdim}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^n)=p^{n-1}+1$ (the generator acts by a unipotent matrix, and a unipotent matrix of order $p^n$ needs a Jordan block of size $>p^{n-1}$, which is also enough), and $\operatorname{rdim}_k((\mathbb{Z}/p)^n)=2$ (a one-dimensional representation of a $p$-group is trivial, and an $\mathbb{F}_p$-subspace of $(k,+)$ embeds in the unipotent group $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&*\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$), whereas $\operatorname{ed}_k((\mathbb{Z}/p)^n)=1$ (for a finite subgroup $\Gamma\subset(k,+)$ the additive polynomial $P_\Gamma(x)=\prod_{\gamma\in\Gamma}(x-\gamma)$ is an isogeny with kernel $\Gamma$, so every $\Gamma$-torsor over $F$ has a class $a\in F$ and descends to $k(a)$) and $\operatorname{ed}_k(\mathbb{Z}/p^n)\le n$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:versal}). The natural envelope is the embedding $\mathbb{Z}/p^n\hookrightarrowW_n$ by Witt translation (Section~\ref{ss:gen}), which restricts on $\langle g^{p^j}\rangle$ to the Witt translation of $W_{n-j}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:intermediate}). With $\dimW_{n-j}$ in place of $\operatorname{rdim}$ the subgroup formula reads
\[
\operatorname{ed}^{[p^j]}_k(\tau_{\mathrm{gen}})=\dimW_{n-j}=n-j\qquad(0\le j\le n),
\]
which is Ledet's conjecture at every level (Questions~\ref{Q2} and~\ref{Q3}; the case $j=n-2$ is Theorem~\ref{thm:N1}): Proposition~\ref{prop:trunc} gives ``$\le$'', and by Proposition~\ref{prop:intermediate} the fixed field $K_j$ realises exactly $n-j$ iff Ledet's conjecture holds for $\mathbb{Z}/p^{n-j}$. One template thus covers both regimes: the profile at degree $d$ is the minimal envelope dimension over subgroups of index $\le d$. In the Karpenko--Merkurjev setting it is proved on the prime-to-$p$ plateau (\cite[Proposition~\ref{A-prop:KMplateau}]{PA}) and, for abelian $G$ of exponent $p^a$ with $\mu_{p^a}\subset k$, in all degrees ([A,\,\ref{A-cor:subgroupabelian}]); in general it is open in $p$-power degrees in both settings.
